description: A double waterfall in a monsoon forest pocket, with a lookout above and a staircase down to the plunge pool.

title: Find your own tier at the Buley Rockholes
description: A cascade of small waterfalls and rock spas stepping down the creek - you can usually claim a pool to yourselves.

title: Walk among the Magnetic Termite Mounds
description: Thin wedge-shaped mounds all aligned north-south to manage temperature - a whole field of them, some over a century old.

title: Sit through a Top End build-up storm in Darwin
description: Australia's most tropical and most multicultural capital, rebuilt twice - after the 1942 bombings and after Cyclone Tracy in 1974.

title: Eat laksa and watch sunset at Mindil Beach Sunset Market
description: Thursday and Sunday in the dry season, everyone carries dinner onto the sand for the sunset. The laksa queues are long for good reason.

title: Swim safely in the Darwin Waterfront wave lagoon
description: You cannot swim in the sea here because of crocodiles and box jellyfish - so the city built a netted lagoon and a wave pool instead.

title: Stand in the Cyclone Tracy sound room at MAGNT
description: A darkened room playing the actual recording of Tracy hitting Darwin on Christmas Eve 1974. Also home to Sweetheart, a 5m stuffed crocodile.

title: Get in the Cage of Death at Crocosaurus Cove
description: A clear acrylic cylinder lowered into a saltwater crocodile enclosure, in the middle of the Darwin CBD.

title: Visit the Tiwi Islands on a permit day tour
description: Bathurst and Melville Islands, 80km north of Darwin - a distinct culture, strong art centres, and a football grand final that stops the islands.

title: Use Katherine as your base between the Centre and the Top End
description: Jawoyn and Dagoman country, at the crossroads of the Stuart and Victoria Highways, and the gateway to Nitmiluk.

title: Canoe between the walls of Nitmiluk Gorge
description: Thirteen sandstone gorges separated by rapids, on Jawoyn land - you portage the canoe between them as you work upstream.

title: Take the two-gorge cruise at Nitmiluk
description: The easy way to see the gorge - a boat to the first gorge, a short walk over the rocks, then a second boat beyond the rapids.

title: Sit in the Katherine Hot Springs after a long drive
description: Free thermal pools on the edge of town, around 32 degrees, shaded by paperbarks. Closed in the wet when the river runs high.

title: Swim the upper pools at Edith Falls
description: Leliyn - a large lower pool most people stop at, and a steep 2.6km loop up to smaller, better, emptier pools above it.

title: Visit the Nyinkka Nyunyu art centre at Tennant Creek
description: A Warumungu-run cultural centre built around a sacred site, with one of the most honest local history displays in the country.

title: Camp overnight at Karlu Karlu, the Devils Marbles
description: Enormous granite boulders split and rounded by heat, sacred to the Warumungu, Kaytetye, Alyawarra and Warlpiri - and a first-rate campsite.

title: Add something to the ceiling of the Daly Waters Pub
description: An outback pub covered inside with decades of hats, licence plates, ID cards and underwear left by travellers, plus a nightly beef and barra.

title: Float in the Mataranka thermal pool
description: Around 34 degrees year-round, in a palm forest - the country of We of the Never Never, with a replica homestead on site.

title: Drift down the current at Bitter Springs
description: Better than the Mataranka pool a few kilometres away - a slow thermal stream you float down with a pool noodle and then walk back up.

title: Watch the cliffs light up at Rainbow Valley
description: Banded sandstone bluffs that turn from ochre to violet at sunset, an hour south of Alice down a sandy track. Almost nobody goes.

title: Drive the Savannah Way across the Top End
description: The route linking Cairns to Broome through Katherine - gorges, hot springs and roadhouses, and long stretches with no fuel.

title: Drive the Stuart Highway from Darwin to the Red Centre
description: The Track - 2,700km following Stuart's 1862 crossing and the old Overland Telegraph Line, straight up the middle of the continent.

title: Loop the Red Centre Way including the Mereenie Loop
description: Alice to Uluru the long way, through the West MacDonnells and Kings Canyon. The Mereenie section is unsealed and needs a permit.

title: Four-wheel-drive the riverbed into Finke Gorge
description: The access track runs along the sandy bed of the Finke River itself - high clearance 4WD only, and never after rain.

title: Find the red cabbage palms in Palm Valley
description: About 3,000 Livistona mariae palms survive here and nowhere else on earth - a relic of when the Centre was rainforest.

title: Walk a section of the Larapinta Trail
description: 223km along the spine of the West MacDonnells in twelve sections - you can walk one section in a day or the whole thing in two weeks.

title: Camp in Trephina Gorge in the East MacDonnells
description: Quartzite walls and river red gums east of Alice, including one of the largest ghost gums in Central Australia. Far quieter than the west.

title: Learn dot painting from Anangu artists at Maruku Arts
description: An Anangu-owned collective at Uluru running workshops where the artists explain what the symbols actually mean, through an interpreter.

title: Walk on the roof of Australian Parliament House
description: Built into Capital Hill so the public can literally stand above the politicians - free entry, and you can sit in on Question Time.

title: Stay for the Last Post ceremony at the Australian War Memorial
description: Every day at closing, one name from the Roll of Honour is read out. It takes fifteen minutes and it undoes most people.

title: See the Holden prototype and Azaria's story at the National Museum
description: A deliberately unconventional building on Acton Peninsula, telling Australian social history through objects rather than dates.

title: Stand in front of Blue Poles at the National Gallery
description: Pollock's Blue Poles caused a national scandal when bought for $1.3m in 1973 - it is now among the most valuable paintings in the country.

title: Find someone you recognise at the National Portrait Gallery
description: Australia told through the faces of about 400 people, from Bennelong to Cathy Freeman, in a purpose-built 2008 gallery.

title: Drop down the free-fall slide at Questacon
description: The national science centre, with around 200 hands-on exhibits and a 6m vertical slide you go down on your stomach.

title: Walk the Himalayan Cedar forest at the National Arboretum
description: 250 hectares planted with 94 forests of rare and endangered trees from around the world, started after the 2003 bushfires.

title: Walk the Rainforest Gully at the Australian National Botanic Gardens
description: The most complete living collection of Australian native plants anywhere, on the slope of Black Mountain.

title: Cycle the full circuit of Lake Burley Griffin
description: An artificial lake at the centre of Griffin's city plan, with a 28km bridge-to-bridge loop linking most of the national institutions.

title: See Griffin's city plan laid out from Mount Ainslie
description: The lookout that shows why Canberra looks the way it does - a straight line runs from here through the War Memorial to Parliament House.

title: Go up Black Mountain Tower for the 360-degree view
description: Telstra Tower stands 195m on top of Black Mountain, giving the highest public view over the whole territory.

title: See the Sidney Nolan Sunday paintings at Canberra Museum and Gallery
description: The local museum rather than a national one - social history of the region, and a dedicated Nolan collection.

title: Blow your own glass at Canberra Glassworks
description: Australia's only cultural centre dedicated to glass, in the restored 1915 Kingston Powerhouse - book a Make Your Own session.

title: Stand in the old House of Representatives at the Museum of Australian Democracy
description: Whitlam was dismissed on these steps in 1975. The building is preserved as it was, down to the ashtrays in the party rooms.

title: See Cook's Endeavour journal at the National Library
description: The Treasures Gallery rotates original documents - Cook's journal, Bradman's scorebooks, early maps of the continent.

title: Strike your own coin at the Royal Australian Mint
description: Every circulating Australian coin is made here - watch the production floor from a gallery, then press your own $1 on the visitor machine.

title: Do a Zooventure meet-the-animals tour at the National Zoo
description: A privately run zoo and aquarium on Lake Burley Griffin, unusually willing to get you inside enclosures with keepers.

title: Walk among the skeletons at the National Dinosaur Museum
description: A private collection in Gungahlin with one of the largest permanent dinosaur displays in the country, plus an outdoor garden.

title: Ride the alpine slide at Corin Forest
description: A 1.2km bobsled-style toboggan run down a forested hillside 45 minutes from the city, plus snow play in winter.

title: Look for platypus at the Sanctuary in Tidbinbilla
description: A predator-fenced wetland sanctuary with platypus, brush-tailed rock wallabies and koalas - and the Deep Space Communication Complex next door.

title: Find the rock art at Yankee Hat in Namadgi
description: Namadgi covers nearly half the ACT. A flat 6km walk across a frost hollow leads to a Ngunnawal shelter painted with people and animals.

title: Climb the boulders at Square Rock in Namadgi
description: A 9km return walk through snow gums to a granite tor with a boardwalk out onto the top, looking over the Brindabellas.

title: Climb Gibraltar Peak above Tidbinbilla
description: A steep 6.5km return climb to a granite summit at 1,038m, looking straight down into the Tidbinbilla valley.

title: Reach Bimberi Peak, the highest point in the ACT
description: 1,913m, in declared wilderness with no marked track for much of the way - navigation, fitness and a weather window all required.

title: Cross the Tharwa Bridge, the oldest in the ACT
description: An 1895 Allan truss bridge over the Murrumbidgee at the territory's oldest village, on the way into Namadgi.

title: Tour the 1859 Lanyon Homestead
description: A convict-built pastoral homestead on the Murrumbidgee with the Brindabellas behind it - one of the best preserved in the country.

title: See the burnt-out domes at Mount Stromlo Observatory
description: The 2003 firestorm destroyed five telescopes here. The ruins were left standing, and the site still runs public astronomy nights.

title: See whether there is any water in Lake George
description: Just over the NSW border on the Federal Highway - a lake that periodically empties completely, then refills, with a wind farm along its ridge.

title: Taste cool-climate Shiraz in the Canberra wine region
description: Around Murrumbateman, half an hour north - high altitude Shiraz and Riesling, and the source of Clonakilla's Shiraz Viognier.

title: Spend a Sunday at the Old Bus Depot Markets
description: A 1920s bus depot in Kingston full of makers and food stalls every Sunday - the reliable answer to a Canberra weekend.

title: Set foot in all eight states and territories together
description: The big one. Six states and two territories - tick it off properly, with a photo in each.

title: Drive across the Nullarbor
description: 1,200km between Ceduna and Norseman, including the longest straight stretch of road in Australia at 146.6km. Carry water and watch the fuel gaps.

title: Drive the Explorer's Way from Adelaide to Darwin
description: 3,000km from the Southern Ocean to the Timor Sea, through the Flinders, Coober Pedy, the Red Centre and the Top End.

title: Ride The Ghan from end to end
description: Adelaide to Darwin over about 54 hours, named for the Afghan cameleers who ran the inland routes before the railway.

title: Ride the Indian Pacific coast to coast
description: Sydney to Perth across four days, including the 478km dead-straight Nullarbor section - the longest stretch of straight railway on earth.

title: See sunrise on the east coast and sunset on the west, same day
description: The time difference makes it just possible - dawn at Cape Byron, a flight west, and the sun going down over the Indian Ocean the same evening.

title: Swim in the Pacific, the Indian and the Southern Ocean
description: Three different oceans touch this continent. Bondi, Cottesloe and anywhere along the South Australian or Victorian coast will do it.

title: See a platypus in the wild
description: Harder than it sounds - they are shy, mostly crepuscular, and easy to mistake for a ripple. Eungella and Tidbinbilla are the best odds.

title: Find a wild echidna in the bush
description: Australia's most widespread native mammal and still a genuine thrill to stumble across. Watch the roadsides on warm days after rain.

title: Watch whales on the east coast and the west coast
description: Humpbacks run up both sides of the continent every winter - Hervey Bay on one side, Exmouth or Albany on the other.

title: Stand in falling snow in Australia
description: Australia has more alpine snow country than Switzerland in a good year. Thredbo, Falls Creek or kunanyi will all deliver it.

title: Spend a night somewhere with no phone reception
description: Not difficult in this country, and worth doing deliberately at least once. Tell someone where you are going first.

title: See the core of the Milky Way with no light pollution
description: The galactic core sits high in southern skies from about April to September. Warrumbungle, Arkaroola or anywhere in the Centre.

title: Photograph a Big Thing in every state
description: There are more than 150 of them - Banana, Koala, Merino, Lobster, Pineapple. A genuinely stupid and genuinely great national tradition.

title: Visit a World Heritage site in every state and territory
description: Australia has twenty World Heritage properties, and at least one in every state and territory - Uluru, Kakadu, the Reef, Naracoorte, Port Arthur, Purnululu.

title: Stand on the highest point of a state or territory
description: Kosciuszko is the easy one at 2,228m. Bimberi, Ossa, Bogong, Zeil, Bartle Frere and Meharry get progressively harder.

title: Watch a footy game in a state that isn't yours
description: AFL at the MCG or Adelaide Oval, NRL in Brisbane or Sydney - the code changes at the border and so does the entire atmosphere.

title: Sail through the Hole in the Rock at Piercy Island
description: Motukokako, a sea-carved arch at the tip of Cape Brett that boats pass through when the swell allows. Dolphins are common on the run out.

title: Stand on the Treaty grounds at Waitangi
description: Where the Treaty was signed in 1840 - the founding document of New Zealand, and still the country's most argued-over. The guided tour is worth it.

title: Walk the Cape Brett Track to the lighthouse
description: 16km each way along a knife-edge peninsula to a hut beside the lighthouse. Eight hours in, and the only easy way out is by boat.

title: Kayak to the Haruru Falls through the mangroves
description: A horseshoe waterfall reached by paddling up the Waitangi River - go on an incoming tide and let the water do the work.

title: Wander the old whaling port of Russell
description: Once called the hell hole of the Pacific, now the quietest place in the bay - Christ Church still carries musket holes from 1845.

title: Watch two oceans collide at Cape Reinga
description: Te Rerenga Wairua, where Maori believe spirits depart - and where the Tasman Sea visibly meets the Pacific in a line of standing waves.

title: Sandboard the Te Paki dunes
description: Giant dunes at the top of Ninety Mile Beach that you climb on foot and come down on a boogie board, considerably faster than expected.

title: Drive the length of Ninety Mile Beach
description: A gazetted highway on sand, actually about 88km. Rental agreements almost always forbid it - the safe way is the bus that does it daily.

title: Swim at Matai Bay on the Karikari Peninsula
description: Twin white-sand coves in a DOC reserve, sheltered from almost every wind direction, with a campground behind the dunes.

title: Stand beneath Tane Mahuta in Waipoua Forest
description: The largest living kauri, roughly 51m and possibly 2,000 years old. Scrub your boots at the station - kauri dieback is spread by soil on footwear.

title: Sandboard the Hokianga dunes at Opononi
description: A boat drops you at the giant dunes across the harbour mouth, and you slide back down toward the water. Opononi is where Opo the dolphin lived in 1955.

title: Dive the Poor Knights Islands
description: Cousteau rated this among the world's top dives - a subtropical current brings species found nowhere else this far south, into drowned volcanic caves.

title: Walk to the top of Whangarei Falls
description: A 26m curtain over a basalt lip, with a loop track that puts you at the top, the bottom and behind the spray in about forty minutes.

title: Snorkel the marine reserve at Goat Island
description: New Zealand's first marine reserve, protected since 1975 - snapper come close enough to touch because nobody has fished them in fifty years.

title: Surf the point at Sandy Bay, Tutukaka
description: The most consistent beach break on the Tutukaka Coast, with a long right-hander off the northern rocks when a swell is running.

title: Walk the Mangawhai Cliffs clifftop loop
description: Up onto the cliffs and back along the beach - the return leg only works at low tide, so check the table before you start.

title: Climb the crater rim of Rangitoto
description: Auckland's youngest volcano, erupted about 600 years ago and visible from everywhere in the city. A scoria climb through the largest pohutukawa forest on earth.

title: Hear the dawn chorus on Tiritiri Matangi
description: A predator-free island replanted by volunteers, now holding takahe, kokako and saddleback. Stay the night and the dawn chorus is genuinely startling.

title: Cycle between the vineyards on Waiheke Island
description: Forty minutes by ferry from downtown Auckland to an island of Bordeaux-style reds, olive groves and beaches. Hilly - take the e-bike.

title: Walk the black sand at Piha
description: Iron sand that gets painfully hot, a serious rip, and Lion Rock in the middle of it. Swim between the flags - this beach earns its reputation.

title: Watch the gannet colony at Muriwai
description: Around 1,200 pairs of takapu nesting on a headland stack, close enough that you can watch a chick being fed from the viewing platform.

title: Find the waterfall at Karekare
description: The beach from The Piano, and a short walk inland to a fall dropping into a swimming hole. Check current kauri dieback track closures before going.

title: Jump off the Sky Tower
description: A 192m base-wire jump off the tallest building in the Southern Hemisphere, at 85km/h, landing on a target in the plaza below.

title: Climb Maungawhau for the volcanic field view
description: Mount Eden, the highest of Auckland's 53 volcanoes, with a 50m crater on top. Walking into the crater is prohibited - it is a sacred site.

title: See the Maori court at Auckland Museum
description: Holds Hotunui, a carved meeting house from 1878, and Te Toki a Tapiri, the last great Maori war canoe - 25m from a single totara.

title: Take the ferry to Devonport and walk up North Head
description: Twelve minutes across the harbour to a Victorian village, then up a headland honeycombed with tunnels and gun emplacements from the 1880s Russian scare.

title: Eat your way through the Auckland Fish Market
description: A working auction floor with eating houses built around it - the snapper and the Bluff oysters in season are the reason to come.

title: Have a pint at the Green Dragon in Hobbiton
description: The only permanent set left standing from the films - 44 hobbit holes on a working sheep farm, rebuilt in wood and plaster to last.

title: Float under the glowworms in the Waitomo Caves
description: A boat drifts in silence beneath a ceiling of Arachnocampa luminosa found nowhere else on earth. The guides ask for quiet, and it matters.

title: Black-water raft through the Ruakuri cave system
description: Abseil in, then float an underground river on an inner tube through the dark with glowworms overhead. Cold, wet and genuinely exhilarating.

title: Walk the Marokopa Falls track
description: A 36m fall through a limestone gorge on the road west of Waitomo, with the Mangapohue natural bridge and Piripiri Cave on the same drive.

title: Learn to surf the point break at Manu Bay
description: One of the longest and most reliable left-hand point breaks in the world, and the wave that made Raglan famous through The Endless Summer.

title: Walk in behind Bridal Veil Falls
description: Waireinga drops 55m off a basalt lip in a single clean column, with viewing platforms at the top, halfway down and at the plunge pool.

title: Dig your own hot pool at Hot Water Beach
description: Geothermal water rises through the sand for two hours either side of low tide - bring a spade and get there early to claim a patch.

title: Walk to Cathedral Cove
description: A limestone arch joining two beaches. Cyclone Gabrielle wrecked the access track in 2023 and repairs have run for years - check DOC before you drive out.

title: Ride the Driving Creek Railway
description: A narrow-gauge line the potter Barry Brickell built by hand over 35 years to haul clay, climbing through replanted native bush to the Eyefull Tower.

title: Walk the Karangahake Gorge tunnel and tramway
description: A 1km unlit rail tunnel, swing bridges and the ruins of a gold battery, in a gorge that was one of the richest goldfields in the country.

title: Climb the Pinnacles from the Kauaeranga Valley
description: Up old kauri-logging packhorse steps to a hut, then a ladder scramble to a rock summit for sunrise over both coasts of the peninsula.

title: Walk through the themed gardens at Hamilton Gardens
description: Not a botanic collection but a set of fully enclosed period gardens - Italian Renaissance, Japanese, Indian Char Bagh, and a Tudor knot garden.

title: Watch 220,000 litres a second go through Huka Falls
description: The Waikato River squeezes from 100m wide into an 15m granite chute. The volume is the point - it is less a waterfall than a firehose.

title: Kayak to the Mine Bay Maori rock carvings
description: A 14m carving of Ngatoroirangi cut into the cliff in the late 1970s, reachable only by boat or kayak across Lake Taupo.

title: Soak in the free hot stream at Otumuheke
description: A geothermal stream runs into the cold Waikato River, so you can find whatever temperature you like where the two mix. Free, and busy for good reason.

title: Skydive over Lake Taupo
description: One of the cheapest and busiest drop zones anywhere, over a lake the size of Singapore with three volcanoes on the horizon.

title: Walk to the Tokaanu thermal pools
description: A boardwalk over mud pools and silica terraces at the southern end of the lake, with private thermal baths in the village for a few dollars.

title: Watch the Champagne Pool steam at Wai-O-Tapu
description: A 65m-wide hot spring rimmed in orange arsenic and antimony, plus the Artist's Palette and a geyser that is prompted with soap at 10.15 each morning.

title: See Pohutu geyser erupt at Te Puia
description: The largest active geyser in the Southern Hemisphere, up to 30m, alongside the national carving and weaving schools in Te Whakarewarewa.

title: Eat a hangi cooked in the ground at Whakarewarewa
description: A village where people still cook in steam boxes and bathe in the hot pools they were born beside - guided by the residents themselves.

title: Walk the Redwoods Treewalk after dark
description: Suspension bridges strung between 117-year-old Californian redwoods, lit at night by David Trubridge lanterns.

title: Raft the 7m drop at Tutea Falls on the Kaituna
description: The highest commercially rafted waterfall in the world. You go over it forwards, in a raft, and there is no gentle option.

title: Ride the luge down Mount Ngongotaha
description: A gondola up and a wheeled gravity cart back down, on three tracks of increasing recklessness, above Lake Rotorua.

title: Bathe in the lakeside pools at Polynesian Spa
description: Acidic and alkaline springs fed into separate pools on the edge of the lake - the Priest Spring has been used for its minerals since 1878.

title: See the buried village at Te Wairoa
description: Buried by the 1886 Tarawera eruption that also destroyed the Pink and White Terraces - excavated houses and a waterfall walk behind.

title: Walk the crater floor at Waimangu
description: The only geothermal system on earth created entirely within recorded history, by the 1886 eruption - including Frying Pan Lake, the world's largest hot spring.

title: Cross Orakei Korako by boat to the hidden valley
description: Reachable only by a short ferry across the Waikato - silica terraces, geysers, and Ruatapu Cave with a pool at the bottom of it.

title: Kayak to the hot waterfall on Lake Tarawera
description: Paddle to Hot Water Beach on the far shore, where thermal water seeps up through the sand under the mountain that erupted in 1886.

title: Swim between the Blue and Green Lakes
description: Tikitapu and Rotokakahi sit side by side in visibly different colours. Rotokakahi is tapu and closed to the public - swim in Tikitapu only.

title: Climb Mauao at Mount Maunganui for sunrise
description: 232m straight up off the end of the peninsula, with ocean beach on one side and harbour on the other. Locals do it before work.

title: Soak in the saltwater hot pools at the base of Mauao
description: Geothermal saltwater drawn from 600m below, in pools right at the foot of the mount - the obvious reward after climbing it.

title: See Whakaari from the water or the air
description: New Zealand's most active volcano, 48km offshore. Landings ended after the 2019 eruption killed 22 people - boat and flight tours view it from a distance.

title: Swim at Ohope Beach
description: 11km of sand facing north into the Bay of Plenty sun, repeatedly voted the country's best beach and still relatively quiet.

title: Watch the world's first sunrise from the East Cape Lighthouse
description: 800 steps up the easternmost point of mainland New Zealand - among the first inhabited places on earth to see each new day.

title: Walk to the end of Tolaga Bay wharf
description: 660m of concrete pier built in 1929, the longest in the country, running out into open sea because there was no harbour to build in.

title: Slide down the Rere Rockslide
description: A 60m natural rock chute in the Wharekopae River that locals ride on boogie boards and truck inner tubes. Bring padding - it is rock.

title: Walk behind Rere Falls
description: A 20m-wide curtain with a dry ledge behind it, five minutes upstream from the rockslide on the same road.

title: Drink Chardonnay where the grapes ripen first
description: The country's Chardonnay capital and the first major wine region to be harvested each year, on fertile Poverty Bay flats.

title: Walk the art deco streets of Napier
description: Flattened by an earthquake in 1931 and rebuilt in two years, entirely in the style of the moment - one of the most complete art deco towns anywhere.

title: Visit the gannet colony at Cape Kidnappers
description: The largest mainland gannet colony on earth, on a cliff at the end of an 8km beach walk that is only passable at low tide.

title: Watch the sun go down from Te Mata Peak
description: 399m of limestone ridge you can drive or walk up, looking across the Heretaunga Plains to Ruapehu on a clear day.

title: Cycle the Hawke's Bay wine trails
description: New Zealand's oldest wine region and its best for Syrah and Bordeaux blends, linked by 200km of flat off-road cycle trail.

title: Photograph Mount Taranaki reflected in the Pouakai Tarns
description: The reflection shot everyone wants, and it needs a windless morning after a wet night. The tarn is small and the walk in is long and steep.

title: Walk the Pouakai Crossing
description: 19km across the flanks of the volcano through goblin forest, swamp and alpine tops. Quieter than Tongariro and arguably more varied.

title: Walk to Dawson Falls on Mount Taranaki
description: An 18m fall over an old lava flow, ten minutes from the road, on the mountain's south side where the forest is thickest.

title: Cycle the New Plymouth Coastal Walkway to the Wind Wand
description: 13km of seafront path past Len Lye's 45m kinetic Wind Wand and the Te Rewa Rewa bridge, which frames the mountain exactly.

title: See the kinetic sculpture at the Len Lye Centre
description: A mirrored stainless steel building holding the work of a New Zealander who spent his life making sculpture that moves, and film scratched by hand.

title: Drive Surf Highway 45 around the mountain
description: 105km of coast road with a break at almost every river mouth, and the volcano over your shoulder the entire way.

title: Walk the Tongariro Alpine Crossing
description: 19.4km past the Emerald Lakes and Red Crater, often called the best day walk in the country. Shuttle booking is compulsory, and the weather turns fast.

title: Ski Whakapapa on an active volcano
description: The North Island's largest ski area, on the slopes of Ruapehu, which last erupted in 2007 and has a crater lake at the top.

title: Ride the Old Coach Road between the viaducts
description: A cobbled 1906 coach road relaid as a cycle trail, passing the Hapuawhenua viaduct - the last surviving curved timber-era viaduct in the country.

title: Canoe the Whanganui Journey to the Bridge to Nowhere
description: Five days down a river that holds legal personhood in its own right, to a 1936 concrete bridge in the bush leading nowhere at either end.

title: Ride the Durie Hill elevator through the hillside
description: You walk 200m into a tunnel, then ride a 1919 public elevator 66m up inside the hill - the only one of its kind in the country.

title: Walk the Te Apiti Manawatu Gorge track
description: A river gorge cutting straight through the ranges, with the Te Ahu a Turanga sculpture above it and a wind farm along the ridge.

title: See the colossal squid at Te Papa
description: Free entry to the national museum, holding the only intact colossal squid on display anywhere and the Gallipoli figures Weta made at 2.4 times life size.

title: Hear kaka and kiwi at Zealandia
description: 225 hectares behind a predator-proof fence, ten minutes from parliament, on a 500-year plan to return the valley to how it was before people arrived.

title: Ride the cable car up to the Botanic Garden
description: Running since 1902 from Lambton Quay to Kelburn, with the best view of the harbour at the top and a walk back down through the gardens.

title: Take the Weta Workshop tour
description: Where the props, armour and creatures for Lord of the Rings were actually made - in an unremarkable suburban shed in Miramar.

title: Walk out to the Red Rocks seal colony
description: A rough coast track from Owhiro Bay to red-stained volcanic rock where male fur seals haul out over winter. Keep 20m back.

title: Climb Mount Victoria for the harbour view
description: 196m above the city with the whole harbour laid out, and the town belt below it doubling as the forest the hobbits hid in from the Black Rider.

title: Drink your way along Cuba Street
description: Wellington roasts and drinks more coffee per head than anywhere else in the country, and this street is where it concentrates.

title: Spend a day on predator-free Kapiti Island
description: A nature reserve cleared of rats since 1998, where takahe walk past you on the track. Numbers are capped daily and permits book out.

title: Take the ferry to Matiu Somes Island
description: A quarantine station, then an internment camp in both wars, now a predator-free reserve with tuatara - twenty minutes out into the harbour.

title: Taste Pinot Noir in Martinborough
description: A village laid out as a Union Jack, ringed by small Pinot producers close enough together to visit on a bicycle in an afternoon.

title: Walk up to the Putangirua Pinnacles
description: Earth pillars left by 120,000 years of erosion, used as the Paths of the Dead. The streambed route is the good one - go when it is dry.

title: Climb the 1,000 steps at Castlepoint
description: A lighthouse on a reef, a lagoon behind it and Castle Rock rising 162m above - and a horse race run on the beach every March.

title: Kayak the Abel Tasman coast to Anchorage
description: The smallest national park and the sunniest - golden granite beaches, tidal crossings and a water taxi that lets you walk one way and paddle the other.

title: Cross the Awaroa tidal inlet on foot
description: Passable for about two hours either side of low tide, and impossible otherwise. The beach was bought for the nation by public crowdfunding in 2016.

title: Look into Te Waikoropupu Springs
description: Among the clearest fresh water ever measured, with 63m visibility. The springs are tapu - you look, you do not touch the water.

title: Walk through the Wharariki Beach arches
description: Twenty minutes over farmland and dunes to Archway Islands and seal pups playing in the rock pools. Wind and spray are part of the deal.

title: Walk out along Farewell Spit
description: A 26km sand hook and internationally recognised bird sanctuary - most of it is closed, so the far end is reachable only by licensed tour.

title: Photograph the jetty on Lake Rotoiti
description: Beech forest to the waterline and mountains behind - and eels and trout so used to people they gather under the jetty planks.

title: Climb to Angelus Hut on the Robert Ridge
description: Twelve kilometres along an exposed alpine ridge to a hut beside a tarn in a rock basin. Fully exposed to weather the whole way.

title: Stand at the geographic centre of New Zealand
description: A short steep walk above Nelson to the zero point of the 1870s survey. Not actually the country's centre, but the marker is real enough.

title: See the winning entries at the WOW museum
description: Garments built from wood, bone, wire and rubbish for a competition that started in a Nelson shed in 1987 and now fills a stadium in Wellington.

title: Walk a section of the Queen Charlotte Track
description: 70km of ridge above drowned river valleys, with boats moving your pack between lodges so you walk with nothing on your back.

title: Ride the mail boat through the Pelorus Sound
description: A working delivery run to households with no road access - you ride along while the skipper drops off post, groceries and the occasional sheep.

title: Taste Sauvignon Blanc where the style was invented
description: The first vines went in in 1973 and within twenty years Marlborough Sauvignon had rewritten what the grape could taste like. Flat enough to cycle.

title: See the aircraft collection at Omaka
description: Peter Jackson's WWI aircraft collection, staged by Weta as full crash scenes with mannequins rather than parked in rows.

title: Watch sperm whales surface off Kaikoura
description: A canyon a kilometre deep sits close to shore, so sperm whales feed here year-round - one of the few places on earth you can count on them.

title: Swim with dusky dolphins at Kaikoura
description: Pods of several hundred duskies, and the rule is that you have to entertain them - sing through your snorkel and they will circle you.

title: Eat crayfish off the roadside at Nins Bin
description: A caravan on the coast road selling crayfish pulled from pots you can see from the counter. Kaikoura literally means to eat crayfish.

title: Punt the Avon through the Botanic Gardens
description: A city still visibly rebuilding after 2011, with a punt service on the river running exactly as it did before.

title: Sit in the Cardboard Cathedral
description: A transitional cathedral built from 98 cardboard tubes after the earthquake destroyed the original - designed by Shigeru Ban and meant to last 50 years.

title: Look for Hector's dolphins in Akaroa Harbour
description: A drowned volcanic crater settled by the French in 1840, and home to Hector's dolphin - the smallest marine dolphin, found only in New Zealand.

title: Drive the Summit Road around the crater rim
description: A narrow road along the rim of two extinct volcanoes, looking down into bays on both sides. Mostly unsealed and best not attempted in fog.

title: Walk to the Devils Punchbowl waterfall
description: A 131m fall an hour's walk from the village, in a pass where kea will strip the rubber from your car if you leave it long enough.

title: Ride the TranzAlpine across the Southern Alps
description: Christchurch to Greymouth in about five hours, through 16 tunnels and over five viaducts, with an open-air carriage for the good bits.

title: Scramble the limestone boulders at Castle Hill
description: A field of weathered limestone tors rated among the best bouldering areas anywhere, and named by the Dalai Lama a spiritual centre of the universe.

title: Walk the Hooker Valley Track to Aoraki
description: Three swing bridges and 10km return to a glacial lake with icebergs in it, under the highest mountain in the country. Flat, and the best value walk in New Zealand.

title: Stargaze in the Aoraki Mackenzie Dark Sky Reserve
description: 4,300 square kilometres of protected night sky - one of the largest reserves of its kind, with the Mount John observatory running tours.

title: See Lake Tekapo turn milk blue
description: Glacial flour suspended in the water gives the colour, and the lupins along the shore in November are gorgeous and entirely invasive.

title: Fly onto the Tasman Glacier
description: The longest glacier in the country at 23km, landed on by ski-plane. Its terminal lake did not exist in 1970 and now grows every year.

title: Soak in the thermal pools at Hanmer Springs
description: Sulphur springs found in 1859, now a set of pools at different temperatures in an alpine village surrounded by forestry.

title: Watch the blowholes at Punakaiki Pancake Rocks
description: Limestone stacked in layers by a process still not fully explained, with blowholes that only really perform on a high tide and a westerly swell.

title: Find the Oparara Arches in the Kahurangi forest
description: A 200m limestone arch 43m high over a tannin-stained river, at the end of a rough logging road most visitors never turn down.

title: Ride the Old Ghost Road end to end
description: 85km following a gold miners' road that was surveyed in the 1870s and never finished, completed as a trail 130 years later.

title: See the Denniston Incline
description: Loaded coal wagons were lowered 518m down a 1-in-1.3 gradient by gravity, hauling empties back up. Families lived at the top for decades without a road.

title: Take a heli-hike onto Franz Josef Glacier
description: The glacier has retreated so far that walking onto the ice from the valley ended in 2012 - helicopter access is now the only way onto it.

title: Walk the Fox Glacier valley to the viewpoint
description: The valley track has been repeatedly closed by rockfall and flooding - check DOC's current status, because the road end moves.

title: Catch the reflection at Lake Matheson
description: Aoraki and Tasman mirrored in dark peat-stained water. It needs a still dawn, and the walk around takes about ninety minutes.

title: See the water colour at Hokitika Gorge
description: Rock flour turns the river an almost luminous turquoise between granite walls, crossed by two swing bridges.

title: Watch the sunset at Ship Creek
description: Driftwood piled by the Tasman on a wild beach, with a swamp forest boardwalk behind and almost nobody stopping.

title: Bungy off the Kawarau Bridge
description: The world's first commercial bungy, opened in 1988, 43m into a gorge with the option of touching the water.

title: Climb Ben Lomond above Queenstown
description: 1,748m and about six hours return from town, with the whole Wakatipu basin below and the Remarkables opposite.

title: Ride the TSS Earnslaw across Lake Wakatipu
description: A coal-fired steamship launched in 1912, the same year as the Titanic, still working the lake daily. You can watch the stokers feeding it.

title: Eat a Fergburger at 2am
description: A burger shop with a permanent queue and no marketing budget, open until 5am. It has become the closest thing Queenstown has to a landmark.

title: Jet boat the Shotover canyons
description: Hamilton jets running at 85km/h through canyons narrow enough to touch, with 360-degree spins. A New Zealand invention, used as designed.

title: Walk to the Routeburn Falls hut
description: 32km over the Harris Saddle between two national parks. One of the ten Great Walks, and huts book out the day bookings open.

title: Ride the Skippers Canyon road
description: A gold miners' road cut into a cliff by hand in the 1880s, single lane with no barrier. Almost every rental agreement in the country forbids it.

title: Climb Roys Peak for the ridge photo
description: 1,228m of relentless zigzag up farmland with no shade, to a viewpoint with a queue on it. Closed for lambing from October to mid November.

title: Photograph That Wanaka Tree
description: A crack willow growing out of the lake, originally a fence post that took root. Probably the most photographed tree in the country.

title: Walk to the Rob Roy Glacier
description: Ten kilometres return into a hanging valley where ice calves off the face while you eat lunch. The access road has several fords.

title: Get lost in Puzzling World
description: A three-dimensional maze with 1.5km of passage, a leaning tower and a room where water appears to run uphill. Genuinely good, not just for children.

title: Cycle the Otago Central Rail Trail
description: 152km of old railway through schist country, viaducts and tunnels, at a gradient never steeper than 1 in 50. The trail that started the country's cycle network.

title: Taste Pinot Noir in Bannockburn
description: The southernmost wine region on earth, on gold-sluiced hillsides - continental extremes give the Pinot its structure.

title: Walk up Baldwin Street, the steepest in the world
description: A 1-in-2.86 gradient at its steepest, reclaimed from a Welsh challenger in 2020. Concrete, because asphalt would run downhill in summer.

title: See the albatross colony at Taiaroa Head
description: The only mainland breeding colony of royal albatross anywhere - birds with a three-metre wingspan landing a few metres from the observatory glass.

title: Ride the Taieri Gorge Railway
description: Out of Dunedin's Flemish Renaissance railway station into a gorge crossed by wrought iron viaducts, on a line finished in 1889.

title: Watch yellow-eyed penguins come ashore on the Otago Peninsula
description: Hoiho are among the rarest penguins on earth and will not land if they can see you - which is why the hides here are dug into the hillside.

title: Find the Moeraki Boulders at low tide
description: Septarian concretions that formed on the sea floor 60 million years ago and are now weathering out of the cliff onto the beach.

title: See the Maori rock art at Duntroon
description: Charcoal and ochre drawings under limestone overhangs in the Waitaki valley, some pre-dating European contact by centuries.

title: Cruise Milford Sound to the Tasman Sea
description: Mitre Peak rising 1,692m straight out of the water. It rains about 200 days a year here, and the waterfalls are better when it does.

title: Stay overnight on Doubtful Sound
description: Three times longer and ten times larger than Milford, reached by boat then bus over Wilmot Pass. The skipper cuts the engines for the silence.

title: Drive the Milford Road through the Homer Tunnel
description: 120km past the Mirror Lakes and Monkey Creek into a 1.2km hand-dug tunnel that drops steeply into the Cleddau valley. Avalanche closures are common.

title: Walk the Milford Track
description: 53.5km over Mackinnon Pass past Sutherland Falls, once billed as the finest walk in the world. One direction only, 40 walkers a day, booked out in minutes.

title: Walk the Kepler Track from Te Anau
description: A 60km loop that starts and finishes in town - unusual for a Great Walk - with a long exposed ridge above the bushline in the middle.

title: See the glowworms in the Te Anau caves
description: A living cave system still being carved by an underground river - you go by boat across the lake, then punt through the dark.

title: Look for kiwi in the wild on Rakiura
description: Stewart Island holds around 20,000 tokoeka, which forage in daylight here - the best chance anywhere of seeing a kiwi that nobody put there.

title: Watch the aurora australis from Rakiura
description: Rakiura means glowing skies. At 47 degrees south with a Dark Sky Sanctuary designation, this is the most reliable aurora viewing in the country.

title: Watch sea lions at Nugget Point
description: An 1869 lighthouse on a knife-edge headland above rock stacks, with fur seals, sea lions and elephant seals all hauling out below.

title: Reach Purakaunui Falls in the Catlins
description: A three-tiered 20m fall through podocarp forest, ten minutes from the road, and probably the most photographed waterfall in the south.

title: Stand on the petrified forest at Curio Bay
description: A 180-million-year-old Jurassic forest fossilised in the rock platform, exposed at low tide, with hoiho coming ashore in the next bay.

title: Reach Slope Point, the southernmost tip
description: The southernmost point of the South Island, marked by a signpost and a stand of macrocarpa trees permanently bent sideways by the wind.

title: See Burt Munro's Indian at Invercargill
description: The actual 1920 Indian Scout from The World's Fastest Indian, still held in a hardware shop in town alongside a serious motorcycle collection.

title: Eat Bluff oysters in season
description: Dredged wild from Foveaux Strait for a short season each year, and treated in New Zealand with a seriousness usually reserved for sport.

title: Island-hop the Yasawa chain by boat
description: A 20-island volcanic chain served by one daily catamaran, so you can step off wherever you like and pick it up again days later.

title: Snorkel the reef off a Mamanuca sandbar
description: The islands closest to Nadi, including the sandbar Cloud 9 and the beach used for Cast Away - easy reef access straight off the sand.

title: Slide the natural waterslides at Bouma, Taveuni
description: The Garden Island - three tiers of waterfall in Bouma National Heritage Park, and the Waitavala natural rock slide locals use as a chute.

title: Dive with bull sharks in Beqa Lagoon
description: A shark reserve where up to eight species turn up on one dive, funded by a levy paid to the local villages that gave up fishing rights.

title: Sit in the Sabeto mud pools near Nadi
description: Geothermal mud pools at the foot of the Sleeping Giant, where you coat yourself, dry off in the sun and rinse in a hot spring.

title: Swim the lagoon at Bora Bora
description: A drowned volcano ringed by a barrier reef and motu - the lagoon runs through half a dozen distinct shades of blue in one afternoon.

title: Climb to the Belvedere lookout on Moorea
description: A lookout between Cook's and Opunohu bays, up through pineapple fields, with Mount Rotui splitting the view in two.

title: Watch the surf at Teahupo'o
description: One of the heaviest waves on earth, breaking over shallow reef at the end of the road on Tahiti Iti. Watching is the sensible option.

title: Drift the Tiputa Pass at Rangiroa
description: The second largest atoll in the world - the incoming tide sweeps you through a pass alongside dolphins, grey reef sharks and manta rays.

title: See the wall of sharks at Fakarava
description: A UNESCO biosphere atoll whose south pass holds hundreds of grey reef sharks stacked against the current - among the densest gatherings anywhere.

title: Stand on the rim of Mount Yasur
description: One of the most accessible active volcanoes on earth - you drive most of the way up and watch lava thrown out of the crater after dark.

title: Dive the SS President Coolidge
description: A 200m troopship sunk by friendly mines in 1942, lying in 20-70m of water and reachable from the beach - one of the great shore-accessible wrecks.

title: Swim the blue holes of Espiritu Santo
description: Freshwater springs filtered through limestone to an almost artificial blue, with rope swings over the deepest ones. Nanda and Riri are the best known.

title: Spend a day at Champagne Beach
description: Named for the volcanic gas that bubbles up through the sand at low tide, on a bay of white sand that is quiet unless a cruise ship is in.

title: Swim the natural pool at the Isle of Pines
description: Kanak country, ringed by columnar pines Cook mistook for basalt - the Piscine Naturelle is a reef-enclosed pool you can wade into.

title: Fly over the Heart of Voh
description: A heart-shaped clearing in the mangroves, formed entirely naturally, made famous by Yann Arthus-Bertrand. Only visible from the air.

title: Snorkel the New Caledonia Barrier Reef
description: The second longest double barrier reef in the world, enclosing one of the largest lagoons - World Heritage listed and remarkably intact.

title: Climb down the ladder into To Sua Ocean Trench
description: A 30m swimming hole in a lava field, joined to the sea by a tunnel, reached by a near-vertical wooden ladder. The name means giant swimming hole.

title: Stay in a beach fale at Lalomanu
description: Open-sided thatched huts on the sand, run by the village, with meals included - the cheapest and best way to sleep in Samoa.

title: Watch the Alofaaga blowholes fire
description: Lava tubes on the Savai'i coast that fire seawater tens of metres up. Locals throw coconuts in to show the force - tip them, it is worth it.

title: Swim with humpback whales in Vava'u
description: Tonga is one of very few countries licensing in-water swims with humpbacks, which come here to calve. Strictly regulated and worth every cent.

title: Walk the Mapu'a 'a Vaea blowholes
description: Five kilometres of coastal terrace riddled with blowholes that fire together on a big swell - the name means chief's whistles.

title: Have a Ha'apai island to yourself
description: 62 islands, most uninhabited, with almost no tourism infrastructure - the quietest corner of an already quiet country.

title: Cross the Aitutaki lagoon to One Foot Island
description: A triangular lagoon widely rated the most beautiful anywhere, with a motu whose one-room post office will stamp your passport.

title: Walk the cross-island track past the Needle
description: Straight over the middle of the island past Te Rua Manga, a volcanic plug locals call the Needle. Steep, muddy and about four hours.

title: Snorkel the Muri lagoon
description: A shallow lagoon protected by four motu, warm enough to stay in all day, with a Saturday night market on the beach behind it.

title: Paddle the Marovo Lagoon
description: The largest saltwater lagoon on earth, enclosed by a double barrier reef, with villages that still carve to order in kerosene wood.

title: Dive the wrecks of Iron Bottom Sound
description: More than fifty ships and hundreds of aircraft sank here during the Guadalcanal campaign. Several sit shallow enough to dive on recreational limits.

title: Visit the skull shrines of Skull Island
description: A tiny island in Vonavona Lagoon holding the skulls of Roviana chiefs and their headhunting trophies. Go with a local guide and ask before photographing.

title: Walk the Kokoda Track
description: 96km over the Owen Stanley Range, eight to ten days, following the 1942 campaign. Guided trekking only, and considerably harder than most expect.

title: Kayak the drowned fjords at Tufi
description: Volcanic rias - the only tropical fjords in the world - with village stays on the ridges above and reef diving at the mouths.

title: Travel the Sepik River by canoe
description: 1,100km through haus tambaran spirit houses and some of the most distinctive carving traditions anywhere. Slow, hot, and genuinely remote.

title: Climb Mount Wilhelm
description: At 4,509m the highest point in Papua New Guinea, usually climbed overnight to reach the summit at dawn before the cloud closes in.

title: Float among the stingless jellyfish of Jellyfish Lake
description: A marine lake holding millions of golden jellyfish that lost their sting in isolation. The population has crashed and recovered before - check it is open.

title: Kayak the Rock Islands of Palau
description: 445 undercut limestone islands in a turquoise lagoon, World Heritage listed. Palau requires every visitor to sign an eco-pledge on arrival.

title: Hook onto the current at Blue Corner
description: Routinely voted the best dive site in the world - you clip a reef hook into dead coral and hang in the current while sharks stream past.

title: Swim the chasms at Limu Pools
description: Niue is one raised coral atoll with no rivers, so the sea is startlingly clear - Limu is a set of pools where fresh water seeps in through the rock.

title: Swim with humpbacks off Niue
description: One of the few places permitting in-water encounters, and the whales come within metres of the shoreline drop-off. Population about 1,700 people.

title: Walk the convict ruins at Kingston
description: Part of the same World Heritage convict listing as Port Arthur, and the site of the harshest penal settlement in the system.

title: Take the boat to Phillip Island off Norfolk
description: Stripped bare by introduced rabbits and now slowly revegetating - red and ochre soil, seabird colonies, and a steep scramble to the top.

title: Dive the ghost fleet of Chuuk Lagoon
description: More than 50 Japanese ships and 250 aircraft sunk in two days in 1944, now the largest concentration of wrecks on the seabed anywhere.

title: Explore the basalt city of Nan Madol
description: Around 100 artificial islets built from basalt logs on a reef flat, abandoned by 1800 - a World Heritage site being reclaimed by mangroves.

title: Dive the fleet sunk at Bikini Atoll
description: Warships including the carrier Saratoga, sunk by nuclear tests in 1946. The islanders were removed and have never been able to return permanently.

title: Cycle the length of Majuro atoll
description: A 50km ribbon of land rarely more than a few hundred metres wide, with lagoon on one side and ocean on the other the entire way.

title: Fly-fish the flats of Kiritimati
description: Christmas Island - the largest coral atoll by land area on earth, and among the best bonefish flats anywhere. Also the first place on the planet to see each new year.

title: Reach the Phoenix Islands Protected Area
description: One of the largest and most remote marine protected areas on earth, reachable only by expedition vessel and visited by almost nobody.

title: Snorkel the Funafuti Conservation Area
description: One of the least visited countries on earth - a few thousand tourists a year - and among the most exposed to sea level rise.

title: Walk Command Ridge on Nauru
description: The highest point on the island, with Japanese WWII guns and a view over the phosphate pinnacles left by a century of strip mining.

title: Drive the Quiraing on the Isle of Skye
description: A landslip landscape of pinnacles and hidden plateaus on Skye's Trotternish ridge, reached by a single-track road.

title: Walk up Catbells above Derwentwater
description: England's most-loved fell walk - a short, steep ridge with the whole lake laid out beneath you. Dogs are welcome on the fells.

title: Step across the basalt columns of the Giant's Causeway
description: Around 40,000 interlocking hexagonal columns left by a 60-million-year-old lava flow, at the foot of the Antrim cliffs.

title: Take the Watkin Path up Yr Wyddfa
description: The hardest and quietest of the six routes up Snowdon, starting almost at sea level and finishing on loose scree.

title: Cross the causeway to Mont Saint-Michel at high tide
description: An abbey on a tidal island where the sea can come in faster than a person walks - the tide table is genuinely part of the visit.

title: Kayak the turquoise water of the Verdon Gorge
description: Europe's deepest canyon, 700m at its steepest, filled with water an improbable shade of green from glacial rock flour.

title: Ride the Aiguille du Midi cable car above Chamonix
description: 3,842m in twenty minutes, with a glass box called the Step into the Void hanging over a 1,000m drop.

title: Walk the Tre Cime di Lavaredo loop
description: A 10km circuit around three vertical limestone towers, past WWI tunnels cut into the rock. Dogs are common on Italian trails.

title: Walk between all five villages of the Cinque Terre
description: Five fishing villages stacked on cliffs, linked by coastal path and a train. Sections close after landslides - check before you set out.

title: Sleep in a cave hotel in the Sassi of Matera
description: Continuously inhabited for around 9,000 years, evacuated as a slum in the 1950s, and now a World Heritage city of restored cave dwellings.

title: Get an early ticket for the Nasrid Palaces at the Alhambra
description: The high point of Moorish architecture in Spain - timed entry to the palaces sells out weeks ahead, so book before you book flights.

title: Walk the last 100km of the Camino de Santiago
description: Sarria to Santiago is the minimum distance that earns a Compostela certificate - about five days, and busy in summer.

title: Walk the Cares Gorge in the Picos de Europa
description: A path blasted into a limestone gorge wall for a hydro scheme, 12km each way with a long drop and no handrail.

title: Take the train up the Douro Valley
description: The oldest demarcated wine region on earth, terraced into schist above the river - the line from Porto runs right along the water.

title: Climb to the Moorish Castle above Sintra
description: A hilltop of Romantic palaces in the mist above Lisbon, with a 10th-century castle wall you can walk the length of.

title: Kayak into the Benagil sea cave
description: A domed cave with a circular hole in the roof and its own beach. Swimming to it is dangerous and now restricted - go by boat or kayak.

title: Cross the Bastei Bridge in Saxon Switzerland
description: An 1851 sandstone bridge strung between rock towers 190m above the Elbe, in a national park most visitors to Germany never reach.

title: Cruise the castles of the Rhine Gorge
description: 65km of World Heritage river with around 40 hilltop castles, vineyards on both banks and the Lorelei rock. Dogs travel free on most boats.

title: Walk the East Side Gallery along the Berlin Wall
description: 1.3km of surviving wall painted by 118 artists in 1990 - the longest open-air gallery in the world, and free.

title: Count the waterfalls in the Lauterbrunnen valley
description: 72 waterfalls drop into one glacial valley, including Staubbach falling almost 300m clear of the cliff. Tolkien's Rivendell came from here.

title: Ride the Glacier Express from Zermatt to St Moritz
description: Eight hours, 291 bridges and 91 tunnels, billed as the slowest express train in the world. Dogs travel on a half-fare ticket.

title: Stand above the Aletsch Glacier
description: The largest glacier in the Alps at around 20km long - and visibly, measurably shorter each time anyone goes back.

title: See Hallstatt before the day-trip buses arrive
description: A lakeside village built on 7,000 years of salt mining, and now so overwhelmed by visitors that staying the night is the only way to see it quiet.

title: Drive the Grossglockner High Alpine Road
description: 48km of hairpins to 2,504m below Austria's highest peak. Closed by snow for half the year, and the toll is per vehicle.

title: Ride the 1897 Ferris wheel at the Prater
description: The Riesenrad has been turning since 1897 and is one of the oldest working Ferris wheels anywhere - the park around it is free.

title: Cycle between the nineteen windmills at Kinderdijk
description: Nineteen 18th-century windmills built to drain a polder that sits below sea level - still the largest concentration in the Netherlands.

title: Ride a free white bicycle through Hoge Veluwe
description: A national park that keeps around 1,800 white bikes free for visitors, with a Van Gogh collection in the middle of the heath.

title: See the canals from the water in Amsterdam
description: A World Heritage ring of 17th-century canals, best understood from a small boat rather than the pavement.

title: Hike out onto Trolltunga
description: A rock tongue jutting 700m above a lake, at the end of a 28km return walk that takes most people ten to twelve hours.

title: See the midnight sun over the Lofoten Islands
description: Granite peaks rising straight from the sea above the Arctic Circle, where the sun does not set from late May to mid July.

title: Sail into Geirangerfjord past the Seven Sisters
description: A 15km World Heritage fjord with abandoned farms clinging to ledges and a seven-strand waterfall dropping 250m.

title: Soak in the hot river at Landmannalaugar
description: Rhyolite mountains in yellows and reds around a natural hot spring, reached by a highland road that needs a proper 4x4 and river crossings.

title: Watch icebergs drift out at Jokulsarlon
description: A glacial lagoon that did not exist a century ago, growing as the glacier retreats - the bergs wash up on the black sand opposite.

title: Stand at the foot of Dynjandi in the Westfjords
description: The least visited corner of Iceland - a 100m tiered waterfall, puffin cliffs at Latrabjarg, and roads that close for winter.

title: Climb to the monasteries of Meteora
description: Six working monasteries on top of sandstone pillars, originally reached only by rope ladder and net. Modest dress is enforced.

title: Walk the caldera rim from Fira to Oia
description: 10km along the rim of a flooded volcanic caldera. Do it early - there is no shade and the afternoon sun is brutal.

title: Walk down the Samaria Gorge
description: 16km downhill through a national park gorge that narrows to three metres, ending at a village you can only leave by boat.

title: Walk the cliff path at the Cliffs of Moher
description: 214m of Atlantic cliff with puffins on the ledges from April - the coastal walk from Doolin avoids the visitor centre crowds entirely.

title: Land on Skellig Michael
description: A 6th-century monastery of stone beehive huts up 600 steps on an Atlantic crag. Landings are strictly capped and cancelled in any swell.

title: Drive the Sky Road in Connemara
description: A 16km loop out of Clifden over bog and quartzite hills, with the Twelve Bens inland and the Atlantic on the other side.

title: Cross Charles Bridge before the city wakes up
description: A 1357 stone bridge lined with baroque statues. By nine it is shoulder to shoulder; at six it is yours and the fog is on the river.

title: Find the Pravcicka Gate in Bohemian Switzerland
description: The largest natural sandstone arch in Europe, in a national park that was badly burnt in 2022 and is visibly recovering.

title: Raft the Vltava through Cesky Krumlov
description: A medieval town wrapped in a river bend beneath a castle with live bears in the moat - and you can paddle straight through the middle of it.

title: Walk the boardwalks of Plitvice Lakes
description: Sixteen terraced lakes joined by waterfalls, over 18km of boardwalk. Croatia's oldest national park, and it sells timed tickets in summer.

title: Walk the full circuit of Dubrovnik's walls
description: 2km of intact city wall up to 25m high, looping the old town. Go at opening or an hour before close - the midday heat up there is fierce.

title: Sail the Kornati archipelago
description: 89 mostly bare limestone islands in a national park with almost no permanent residents - Shaw called them a labour of gods.

title: Walk to Morskie Oko in the Tatra Mountains
description: A 9km walk up a sealed road to a glacial lake under 2,000m peaks. Dogs are banned in the Polish Tatra National Park.

title: Look for wild bison in Bialowieza Forest
description: The last large stretch of primeval lowland forest in Europe, and home to the biggest free-roaming European bison population.

title: Walk the largest brick castle in the world at Malbork
description: A 13th-century Teutonic Order fortress covering 21 hectares - by land area the largest castle anywhere, and rebuilt after near-total wartime destruction.

title: Climb the Eiffel Tower stairs instead of queueing for the lift
description: The stair ticket is cheaper and the queue is a fraction of the lift's. 674 steps to the second floor, then a lift for the summit.

title: See the Impressionists in a converted railway station
description: Monet, Degas and Van Gogh hung under the glass roof of the old Gare d'Orsay. The clock face on the top floor looks straight across the Seine.

title: Stand under the rebuilt spire of Notre-Dame
description: Reopened in December 2024 after the fire. Entry to the cathedral is free; book a timed slot online to skip the worst of the wait.

title: Walk the ossuary tunnels beneath the fourteenth arrondissement
description: Two kilometres of tunnel lined with the bones of six million Parisians, moved here when the city closed its overflowing cemeteries in 1786.

title: Walk the Promenade Plantee above the street
description: A garden built along a disused railway viaduct in 1993. New York's High Line copied the idea a decade later.

title: Watch the sunset from the steps of Sacre-Coeur
description: The highest natural point in Paris. Come up through the back streets rather than the crowded funicular side.

title: Eat your way along the Rue Mouffetard market
description: One of the oldest market streets in Paris, best on a Sunday morning when the cheesemongers and rotisseries are all open.

title: See the Louvre at night when the queues have gone
description: Open late on Wednesdays and Fridays. The Denon wing after eight is a different museum to the one at midday.

title: Cycle the Grand Canal in the gardens of Versailles
description: The gardens are vast enough that walking eats the whole day. Hire a bike at the canal and ride out to Marie Antoinette's hamlet.

title: Boulder on the sandstone of Fontainebleau forest
description: The birthplace of modern bouldering. Colour-graded circuits run from a child's scramble to some of the hardest problems in Europe.

title: See the Conde collection at Chateau de Chantilly
description: The second-best collection of old masters in France after the Louvre, in a chateau most day-trippers from Paris never reach.

title: Walk the medieval walls of Provins
description: A complete walled fair town from the twelfth century, an hour from Paris and almost entirely overlooked.

title: Time the lavender bloom on the Valensole plateau
description: The lavender is cut in the third week of July, so late June to mid-July is the window. Go at first light, before the coaches.

title: Walk the ochre trail at Roussillon
description: A short loop through old ochre quarries in seventeen shades of red and yellow. Do not wear white shoes.

title: Stand under the Pont du Gard aqueduct
description: A three-tier Roman aqueduct built without mortar around 50 AD. You can swim in the Gardon river underneath it in summer.

title: Look for pink flamingos in the Camargue
description: Salt lagoons at the mouth of the Rhone, with white horses, black bulls and Europe's largest flamingo colony.

title: Swim in the calanques between Marseille and Cassis
description: Limestone inlets with water the colour of a swimming pool. En-Vau is the classic; the walk in is steep and there is no shade.

title: Take the coast path around Cap Ferrat
description: A free public footpath around a peninsula of private villas. Eleven kilometres if you walk the whole circuit.

title: See the Matisse chapel at Vence
description: Matisse designed every element of it in his eighties and called it his masterpiece. Go on a bright morning for the glass.

title: Drive the Route des Cretes above Cassis
description: The highest sea cliffs in France, on a road that closes on high-wind and fire-risk days. Check before you set out.

title: Ride a boat to the car-free island of Porquerolles
description: Vineyards and white-sand beaches twenty minutes off the Var coast, with no private cars. Hire a bike at the port.

title: Walk into the Ecrins from the Pre de Madame Carle
description: France's wildest high national park, with no ski resorts inside its core. The glacier walk from Pre de Madame Carle is the classic day out.

title: Ride the Train des Pignes up from Nice
description: A narrow-gauge line from the coast up through the back-country gorges to Digne. Locals use it; almost no visitors do.

title: See the Lascaux cave paintings in the facsimile
description: The original cave closed in 1963 to save the pigment. Lascaux IV reproduces it millimetre for millimetre, in the same dark and cold.

title: Canoe the Dordogne beneath the castles
description: A gentle paddle from Vitrac past Beynac and Castelnaud, two castles that spent the Hundred Years War glaring at each other.

title: Climb the Dune du Pilat at sunset
description: The tallest sand dune in Europe at around 100 metres, still moving inland a few metres a year. Atlantic on one side, pine forest on the other.

title: Taste your way through Saint-Emilion
description: A world heritage wine village built over a monolithic church carved out of the rock beneath it.

title: Wait for the mist on the Bordeaux water mirror
description: The largest reflecting pool in the world, on the quay in front of the Place de la Bourse. It fogs over every few minutes.

title: Surf the beach breaks at Hossegor
description: A deep offshore canyon funnels swell straight onto the sand here, which is why the pro tour keeps coming back.

title: Ride the Rhune rack railway above the Basque coast
description: A 1924 wooden cog train up a Basque mountain, with pottok ponies and vultures at the top and both coasts visible on a clear day.

title: Cross the Passerelle d'Holzarte footbridge
description: A wire suspension bridge strung 180 metres above a Basque gorge in 1920 by Italian labourers. Not for the queasy.

title: Cycle the salt marshes of the Ile de Re
description: Over a hundred kilometres of flat cycle path between whitewashed villages, oyster beds and salt pans.

title: Walk the double walls of Carcassonne early
description: Fifty-two towers and three kilometres of wall. Stay the night inside and the place is yours after the last coach leaves.

title: See the prehistoric bison at Niaux
description: One of the few original painted caves still open to visitors. You walk 800 metres into the dark with a lamp to reach the Salon Noir.

title: Cross the Millau Viaduct
description: The tallest bridge in the world, its masts higher than the Eiffel Tower. Stop at the D992 viewpoint rather than photographing it at speed.

title: Paddle the Gorges du Tarn
description: Fifty kilometres of limestone canyon with green water and villages wedged into the base of the cliffs.

title: Stand in the Cirque de Gavarnie
description: A natural amphitheatre 1,500 metres high with the tallest waterfall in France down its back wall.

title: Swim under the Pont du Diable at Saint-Guilhem
description: A medieval pilgrim village at the mouth of a gorge, with swimming holes under an eleventh-century bridge.

title: Ride the Train Jaune through the Cerdagne
description: A canary-yellow open-carriage train climbing to 1,593 metres, the highest railway station in France.

title: Look through the telescopes at the Pic du Midi
description: A working observatory at 2,877 metres that lets a handful of people stay overnight. The Milky Way from the terrace is the reason to do it.

title: Eat cassoulet where it was invented
description: Toulouse, Castelnaudary and Carcassonne have argued over the recipe for centuries. Winter is when it makes sense to eat it.

title: Walk up the Puy de Dome volcano
description: A dormant volcano above Clermont-Ferrand with eighty more lined up behind it. The Chemin des Muletiers is the walking route; there is a rack railway if you would rather.

title: Ride over the highest paved pass in the Alps
description: At 2,764 metres the Iseran only clears of snow for about ten weeks a year, which is the whole point of getting there.

title: Swim in Lac d'Annecy
description: Fed by mountain springs and reckoned the cleanest large lake in Europe. The cycle path around it runs on an old railway line.

title: Paddle under the Pont d'Arc
description: A natural stone arch over the river, then thirty kilometres of gorge with one bivouac site halfway. Book the bivouac before you go.

title: Eat in a certified Lyon bouchon
description: Small bistros serving the offal-heavy cooking Lyon built its name on. Look for the Authentique Bouchon Lyonnais plaque on the door.

title: Find the traboules of Croix-Rousse
description: Covered passageways cut between buildings so silk workers could carry cloth in the dry. Many are still open to the public behind unmarked doors.

title: Drive the cliff road through Combe Laval
description: A road blasted into a vertical limestone wall in the 1890s to bring timber out. Tunnels open straight onto a 600-metre drop.

title: Walk the ridge of the Puy Mary
description: The eroded core of Europe's largest extinct volcano, with radiating valleys you can trace from the summit.

title: Walk the customs path around the Pointe du Raz
description: The old smuggler-watching path along Brittany's western tip, where the Atlantic hits the granite properly.

title: Count the standing stones at Carnac
description: More than three thousand menhirs in rows running four kilometres, raised between 4500 and 3300 BC. Older than Stonehenge.

title: Watch the tide come in at Saint-Malo
description: One of the biggest tidal ranges in Europe. At low water you walk out to Chateaubriand's island tomb; six hours later it is gone.

title: Follow the pink granite coast path
description: Wind-rounded boulders the colour of salmon, piled along the sea between Perros-Guirec and Ploumanac'h.

title: Walk Omaha Beach at low tide
description: Five kilometres of open sand the American landings crossed on 6 June 1944. The American cemetery sits on the bluff above it.

title: See the chalk arch and needle at Etretat
description: The cliffs Monet painted more than twenty times. Walk up to the chapel for the view back along the arch.

title: Stand in Monet's garden at Giverny
description: The lily pond, the green bridge and the wisteria, kept as he planted them. Go at opening or an hour before closing.

title: Cycle the Loire a Velo between the chateaux
description: Nine hundred kilometres of signed, mostly flat cycle route along the last wild river in France, linking Chambord, Chenonceau and Amboise.

title: See the double helix staircase at Chambord
description: Two spirals wound around each other so people going up never meet those coming down. Leonardo is thought to have had a hand in it.

title: Stand on the white cliffs of Cap Blanc-Nez
description: The French half of the same chalk as Dover, with England visible across the strait on a clear day and almost nobody there.

title: Drive the Alsace wine route villages
description: One hundred and seventy kilometres of half-timbered villages and riesling, from Marlenheim down to Thann.

title: Climb to the Chateau du Haut-Koenigsbourg
description: A red sandstone castle restored by Kaiser Wilhelm II, looking out over the whole Rhine plain to the Black Forest.

title: Walk the grand cru vineyards below Vosne-Romanee
description: A public track runs between the most expensive farmland on earth. The Romanee-Conti plot is marked by a plain stone cross.

title: Find the source of the Loue
description: A river arriving fully formed out of the base of a cliff, painted by Courbet, who grew up an hour away.

title: Cross the Passage du Gois before the tide turns
description: A four-kilometre road to the Ile de Noirmoutier that is under the sea twice a day. Rescue towers stand along it for people who misread the tables.

title: Walk a stage of the GR20
description: Reckoned the hardest waymarked trail in Europe: sixteen stages along the spine of Corsica. The northern half is the brutal half.

title: Sail into the Scandola reserve
description: Red porphyry cliffs and sea caves reachable only by boat, with ospreys nesting on the stacks.

title: Swim off the Lavezzi islands
description: A granite archipelago between Corsica and Sardinia with water clear enough to see the bottom at fifteen metres.

title: Stand on the floor of the Colosseum
description: The arena-floor and underground tickets are separate and sell out weeks ahead. Book the full experience or you only see it from the stands.

title: Look up through the open oculus of the Pantheon
description: The largest unreinforced concrete dome ever built, still standing after nineteen centuries. Go when it rains and watch the water fall through the hole.

title: Walk the Appian Way out of the city
description: Original Roman basalt paving, closed to traffic on Sundays. Hire a bike at the park office and ride out past the tombs and aqueducts.

title: See the Sistine Chapel at opening
description: Four kilometres of galleries before you reach the chapel. The first entry slot of the day is the only one that is not shoulder to shoulder.

title: Look through the Aventine keyhole
description: A keyhole in a green door frames St Peter's dome perfectly down an avenue of hedges. There is usually a small queue of people who know.

title: Eat cacio e pepe in Testaccio
description: The old slaughterhouse quarter, and still where Romans eat. Four ingredients, and every trattoria will tell you the others do it wrong.

title: Descend through the layers of San Clemente
description: A twelfth-century basilica on a fourth-century church on a first-century Mithraic temple. You walk down through all three.

title: Climb to the abandoned town of Civita di Bagnoregio
description: A village on a crumbling tufa pillar, reached by a single footbridge. Its nickname is the dying town, and the cliff really is going.

title: Find the hundred fountains at Villa d'Este
description: A Renaissance water garden running entirely on gravity, with an organ that plays using nothing but falling water.

title: Climb Brunelleschi's dome
description: 463 steps up between the inner and outer shells of a dome nobody could explain how to build until he did it.

title: See the David without the queue
description: Book a timed slot; the walk-up line regularly runs two hours. The unfinished Prisoners in the corridor are the better surprise.

title: Cross the Ponte Vecchio before the shops open
description: The only Florence bridge the retreating Germans left standing in 1944. At seven in the morning it is empty and the shutters are still down.

title: Sit in the shell of the Piazza del Campo
description: A sloping brick fan divided into nine segments for the nine merchants who governed Siena. The Palio is run around its edge twice a summer.

title: Drive the cypress roads of the Val d'Orcia
description: The landscape every idea of Tuscany comes from. The road from San Quirico to Pienza at dawn is the one you have seen in photographs.

title: Count the towers of San Gimignano
