description: Fourteen of the original seventy-two medieval tower houses still stand, built by families competing to be tallest.

title: See the leaning tower and then go inside it
description: Climbing it is the part most people skip. The floor tilts under you on the way up, which the photographs cannot convey.

title: Soak in the free hot cascades at Saturnia
description: Sulphur water at 37 degrees pouring over travertine terraces, open all night and free. Go before seven or after dark.

title: Cycle around the island of Elba
description: Napoleon's first exile, and a proper island of granite coves and steep back roads an hour off the Tuscan coast.

title: Get lost in Cannaregio away from San Marco
description: The quarter where Venetians actually live, with the world's first ghetto at its heart and bacari serving cicchetti along the canals.

title: Ride the number 1 vaporetto down the Grand Canal
description: The slow boat that stops everywhere, which is the point. Stand at the back and it costs a fraction of a gondola.

title: Watch glass being blown on Murano
description: The furnaces were moved out to the island in 1291 so they would not burn Venice down. Go to a working studio, not a showroom.

title: See an opera in the Roman arena at Verona
description: A first-century amphitheatre that has staged opera every summer since 1913. The cheap stone steps are the authentic seats.

title: Walk the Alta Via 1
description: One hundred and twenty kilometres north to south through the Dolomites, sleeping in mountain rifugi. Book the huts months ahead.

title: Meet Otzi the iceman
description: A 5,300-year-old man found melting out of a glacier in 1991, kept in a cold cell you view through a small window.

title: Walk the largest high alpine meadow in Europe
description: Fifty square kilometres of rolling pasture at 2,000 metres, with the Sassolungo standing over it. Cars are barred during the day.

title: Drink coffee in a Trieste caffe
description: An Austro-Hungarian port that still orders coffee in its own vocabulary. Ask for a nero and you get an espresso.

title: See the Roman mosaics at Aquileia
description: Seven hundred and fifty square metres of fourth-century mosaic floor under a basilica, walked over on raised glass.

title: Book ahead for the Last Supper
description: Fifteen minutes in a climate-controlled room, twenty-five people at a time. Tickets are released quarterly and go in minutes.

title: Walk the roof of the Duomo di Milano
description: You can walk among the spires and 3,400 statues on the roof. Take the stairs rather than the lift for the better approach.

title: Take the ferry between the Lake Como villages
description: Varenna, Bellagio and Menaggio sit at the fork of the lake, twenty minutes apart by boat and impossible by road in summer.

title: Ride the Bernina Express over the Alps
description: The highest rail crossing in the Alps without a rack, from Tirano up to 2,253 metres and down into Switzerland. World heritage listed.

title: Climb the Mole Antonelliana in a glass lift
description: A lift runs straight up the middle of the dome with no shaft around it, into the tallest museum building in the world.

title: Hunt truffles in the Langhe in autumn
description: White truffle season runs October to December. Go out with a trifolao and his dog at dawn, then eat what you find.

title: Ride the Skyway to Punta Helbronner
description: A rotating cable car to 3,466 metres on the Italian side of Mont Blanc, looking across at the Matterhorn and Gran Paradiso.

title: Walk the coast path to San Fruttuoso
description: A tenth-century abbey in a cove with no road to it. Walk in over the headland from Portofino and take the boat back.

title: Eat focaccia in Genoa before ten in the morning
description: Genoese focaccia is a breakfast food, dipped in cappuccino by people who will not apologise for it.

title: Walk the streets of Pompeii
description: Sixty-six hectares buried by Vesuvius in 79 AD. Go early, take water, and head for the quieter eastern insulae first.

title: See the better-preserved rooms at Herculaneum
description: Buried deeper and hotter than Pompeii, so the timber, doors and upper floors survived. Smaller, and far less crowded.

title: Climb to the crater rim of Vesuvius
description: A twenty-minute walk up cinder from the car park to a still-steaming crater, with the whole bay laid out below.

title: Eat a pizza where it was invented
description: Marinara or margherita, sixty seconds in a wood oven, eaten folded. The queue outside the famous places moves faster than it looks.

title: Walk the Path of the Gods above Positano
description: Eight kilometres along the ridge from Bomerano to Nocelle, six hundred metres above the sea. Walk it downhill westward.

title: Row into the Blue Grotto
description: You lie flat in a rowing boat to get through the entrance. Only worth it in calm seas and midday light.

title: Stand in the Greek temples at Paestum
description: Three Doric temples from the sixth century BC, better preserved than almost anything in Greece, and usually near-empty.

title: Walk the Valley of the Temples at dusk
description: Seven Greek temples along a ridge above the sea. The site opens at night in summer, which is when to go.

title: Walk on the lava fields of Etna
description: Europe's most active volcano, and often erupting mildly enough to approach with a guide. The Sapienza refuge is the usual start.

title: Eat street food at the Ballaro market
description: Panelle, arancine and sfincione shouted at you in Sicilian. Palermo's markets are Arab in layout and still work that way.

title: Sit in the Greek theatre at Syracuse
description: Carved out of the rock in the fifth century BC and still staging Greek tragedy every May and June.

title: Watch Stromboli erupt after dark
description: The volcano has been erupting every twenty minutes or so for two thousand years. Boats sit offshore below the Sciara del Fuoco at night.

title: Walk the baroque staircases of Ragusa Ibla
description: Rebuilt after the 1693 earthquake in one continuous style, stacked down a ridge with 340 steps between the two halves of town.

title: Swim at Cala Goloritze
description: A white pebble cove under a limestone spire, reachable only on foot down a canyon or by boat. Numbers are capped daily.

title: Look inside a nuraghe
description: Bronze Age stone towers found nowhere else on earth. Sardinia has seven thousand of them; this is the one you can go inside.

title: Sleep in a trullo at Alberobello
description: Fifteen hundred conical drystone houses built without mortar so they could be pulled down when the tax inspector came.

title: Swim off the cliffs at Santa Maria di Leuca
description: The heel of Italy, where the Adriatic and Ionian meet and you can see the colour change from the lighthouse.

title: See the baroque stonework of Lecce
description: The local limestone is soft enough to carve like wood and hardens in the air, which is why every facade here is overrun with detail.

title: Fly the Volo dell'Angelo between two villages
description: A steel cable strung between Castelmezzano and Pietrapertosa, crossed lying flat at 120 kilometres an hour.

title: Walk to the basilica at Assisi
description: Giotto's fresco cycle of the life of St Francis, in a double basilica built into the hillside above the Umbrian plain.

title: Stand under the Cascata delle Marmore when they open the gates
description: A Roman-made waterfall of 165 metres, switched on and off to a published timetable because it feeds a power station.

title: Take a boat to the Spiaggia delle Due Sorelle
description: Two limestone stacks off a beach with no road access, under the Conero cliffs. Boats run from Numana in summer.

title: Eat tagliatelle al ragu in Bologna
description: The recipe is lodged with the Bologna chamber of commerce, and it is not spaghetti bolognese. Forty kilometres of porticoes to walk it off.

title: See the Byzantine mosaics at Ravenna
description: Fifth and sixth-century gold mosaic in eight buildings, the best surviving anywhere outside Istanbul.

title: Taste real balsamic in a Modena acetaia
description: Aged twelve to twenty-five years in a loft of shrinking barrels. It costs what it costs for a reason, and it is nothing like the supermarket version.

title: Go inside the Sagrada Familia in the afternoon
description: The western windows are the warm ones. Gaudi started in 1882 and the towers are only now being finished; book a timed entry.

title: Walk the roof terraces of Casa Mila
description: Gaudi's warrior chimneys on an undulating roof with no straight line in it. The night visit includes the rooftop lit up.

title: Find a seat in Park Guell's serpentine bench
description: A failed housing estate turned public park. The monumental zone is ticketed and capped; the woodland above it is free.

title: Eat standing up at the Boqueria before nine
description: The market bars at the back serve breakfast to the stallholders. By eleven it belongs to the tour groups.

title: Walk the ridge above Montserrat monastery
description: A saw-toothed conglomerate massif with a Benedictine monastery halfway up. Take the rack railway and walk down.

title: Follow the Cami de Ronda around the Costa Brava
description: An old coastguard footpath linking coves between Blanes and Portbou. Sant Feliu to Tossa is the stretch to walk.

title: See Dali's own museum at Figueres
description: He designed it, filled it, and is buried under the floor. Easily the strangest major museum in Spain.

title: Walk to the Estany de Sant Maurici
description: Catalonia's only national park: granite peaks, two hundred lakes and no private cars past the gate.

title: Stand in the forest of arches at the Mezquita
description: Eight hundred and fifty columns of a tenth-century mosque with a cathedral dropped into the middle of it. Free entry before nine thirty.

title: Climb the Giralda ramp instead of stairs
description: Thirty-five ramps rather than steps, built so the muezzin could ride a horse to the top of the minaret.

title: See flamenco in a Triana peña
description: The gitano quarter across the river where the form comes from. A peña is a members' club, and most will let you in.

title: Walk the walkways on top of the Setas
description: The largest timber structure in the world, over a Roman excavation. The rooftop walk at sunset costs very little.

title: Look down into the Tajo gorge at Ronda
description: A town split by a hundred-metre gorge and stitched together by an eighteenth-century bridge. Walk down to the bottom for the real view.

title: Walk the Caminito del Rey
description: A metre-wide walkway pinned to a gorge wall a hundred metres up. Rebuilt in 2015 after years as the most dangerous path in Spain.

title: See the sherry bodegas of Jerez
description: The solera system means a glass of fino contains wine from decades of vintages. Tours end in a tasting, as they should.

title: Walk the volcanic coast of Cabo de Gata
description: The driest place in Europe, a protected volcanic coastline of empty beaches and no development. Bring your own water.

title: Look for lynx in Donana
description: Marshland at the mouth of the Guadalquivir holding most of the world's remaining Iberian lynx and half a million wintering birds.

title: Walk up to the Mirador de San Nicolas at sunset
description: The Moorish quarter opposite the Alhambra, and the view across to it as the Sierra Nevada turns pink behind.

title: See Las Meninas in the Prado
description: Velazquez, Goya and Bosch in one building. Free for the last two hours every day, which is exactly when everyone goes.

title: Stand in front of Guernica
description: Picasso would not let it come to Spain until democracy returned. It arrived in 1981 and has not moved since.

title: Eat bocadillo de calamares on the Plaza Mayor
description: A fried squid sandwich in a landlocked city three hundred kilometres from the sea. Madrid does not explain itself.

title: Walk the Retiro at opening time
description: The old royal gardens, with a glasshouse of pure glass and iron and rowing boats on the lake.

title: Walk to La Pedriza above Manzanares
description: A granite badlands of rounded boulders an hour from the city, where Madrid goes climbing at the weekend.

title: Walk under the Segovia aqueduct
description: One hundred and sixty-seven arches of unmortared granite, built around 100 AD and carrying water until the 1970s.

title: Find the frog on the Salamanca facade
description: A small carved frog hidden in the plateresque stonework. Students say finding it unaided means you will pass your exams.

title: See the human fossils at Atapuerca
description: The richest early-human site in Europe, with remains going back 1.2 million years. The dig is open to guided visits.

title: Walk the three-faith quarters of Toledo
description: A synagogue, a mosque and a cathedral within a few hundred metres, in the city where all three coexisted for centuries.

title: See the hanging houses of Cuenca
description: Balconied houses built out over a gorge in the fifteenth century, best seen from the iron footbridge opposite.

title: Stargaze in the Monfrague dark sky reserve
description: A certified starlight reserve that is also the best raptor-watching site in Spain, with black vultures nesting on the Salto del Gitano.

title: Work through the pintxos bars of the Parte Vieja
description: One pintxo and one drink per bar, then move on. The old town has over a hundred and the good ones are standing room only.

title: See the Guggenheim from the river side
description: Gehry's titanium curves turned a dying industrial port around in a decade. The building outside is as much of the point as the art inside.

title: Climb the 241 steps to Gaztelugatxe
description: A hermitage on a rock island joined to the coast by a stone bridge. Free, but you must book a time slot.

title: See the bison at Altamira in the replica cave
description: The first cave art ever recognised as prehistoric, and dismissed as a forgery for twenty years. The neocave reproduces it exactly.

title: Drive up to the Lagos de Covadonga
description: Two glacial lakes at 1,100 metres in the Picos. In summer the road closes to private cars and a shuttle runs instead.

title: Pour Asturian cider from above your head
description: The escanciador pours from arm's length to aerate it, and you drink the small measure straight down. Anything left goes on the floor.

title: Stand at the edge of the Costa da Morte
description: Where the Romans believed the world ended, and where Camino walkers keep going after Santiago to burn their boots.

title: Walk the complete Roman wall at Lugo
description: Two kilometres of third-century wall with a walkway right around the top, the only fully intact Roman circuit anywhere.

title: Take the boat to the Cies Islands
description: A national park with a daily visitor cap and a beach the locals will tell you is the best in the world. Permits book out in July.

title: Walk the route of the encierro when nothing is chasing you
description: Eight hundred and seventy-five metres from the corral to the ring. Doing it on a quiet morning tells you how narrow Estafeta really is.

title: Cycle the badlands of the Bardenas Reales
description: A semi-desert of eroded clay a hundred kilometres from the Pyrenees, with a military bombing range still active in one corner.

title: Walk into the Ordesa canyon
description: A glacial canyon in the high Pyrenees, with the Cola de Caballo waterfall at the head of it. Shuttle bus only in summer.

title: Look for the Mudejar towers of Teruel
description: Brick and glazed-tile towers built by Muslim craftsmen for Christian patrons after the reconquest. Spain's most overlooked provincial capital.

title: Taste in a Rioja bodega built by an architect
description: The Barrio de la Estacion in Haro has the densest concentration of century-old bodegas anywhere, several of them wrapped in modern architecture.

title: Drive the Sa Calobra road
description: Twelve kilometres of hairpins including a full 270-degree loop where the road ties itself in a knot. Cyclists own it at dawn.

title: Walk the dry stone route through the Tramuntana
description: The GR221 links mountain refuges along a world heritage landscape of terraces and olive groves. Spring, before the heat.

title: Walk a stage of the Cami de Cavalls
description: A 185-kilometre bridle path right around Menorca, first cut so mounted patrols could watch for pirates.

title: Watch the sunset over Es Vedra
description: A four-hundred-metre limestone island off the south-west coast, best seen from the cliffs at Cala d'Hort with nothing playing.

title: Watch the stars from Teide
description: Spain's highest point at 3,715 metres, above the cloud layer and inside one of the world's best protected skies. Permits needed for the summit cone.

title: See what Manrique built in the lava
description: A collapsed lava tube turned into a concert hall and pool, with blind albino crabs found nowhere else living in the lagoon.

title: Walk the Ruta de los Volcanes
description: Along the volcanic spine of the island past the 2021 Tajogaite eruption, with both coasts visible most of the way.

title: Walk in the laurel cloud forest of Garajonay
description: A relict forest of the kind that covered the Mediterranean before the ice ages, kept alive by cloud stripping through the trees.

title: Walk the dunes at Corralejo
description: Eleven kilometres of protected white dunes blown in from the Sahara, with Lobos island sitting just offshore.

title: See the Rosetta Stone at the British Museum
description: Free, enormous, and impossible in one visit. Pick three galleries and ignore the rest, or you will see nothing properly.

title: Walk across the Thames on the Tower Bridge glass floor
description: The high walkways were closed for seventy years and reopened with a glass floor forty-two metres above the river.

title: Stand on the Prime Meridian at Greenwich
description: Longitude zero, and the room where the problem of finding it at sea was finally solved by Harrison's clocks.

title: Watch a play standing in the Globe yard
description: Five pounds to stand as a groundling in an open-roofed reconstruction, which is how the plays were written to be watched.

title: Walk the whole of Hampstead Heath to Kenwood
description: Three hundred and twenty hectares of unmanicured London, with swimming ponds open all year and the best free view of the city from Parliament Hill.

title: Eat at Borough Market on a weekday
description: A thousand years of market on the same spot. Saturdays are unbearable; Tuesday lunchtime is the market the traders prefer.

title: Find Sir John Soane's house exactly as he left it
description: An architect's house kept by act of parliament in the arrangement he died with, crammed with sarcophagi and mirrors. Free, and tiny.

title: Ride the whole Elizabeth line end to end
description: Reading to Abbey Wood through tunnels bored under the entire city, past platforms that look like an airport of the near future.

title: Get inside the Stonehenge circle at sunrise
description: Stone circle access is booked separately and outside opening hours, which is the only way to stand among them rather than behind rope.

title: Explore Wells Cathedral and its scissor arches
description: Inverted arches added in 1338 to stop the tower sinking, and an astronomical clock whose jousting knights have run since 1390.

title: Walk the Cheddar Gorge clifftop circuit
description: The deepest gorge in Britain, with a five-kilometre loop along both rims and caves where the oldest complete British skeleton was found.

title: Walk the Jurassic Coast to Durdle Door
description: A limestone arch below a steep chalk path from Lulworth Cove. The whole coast reads as 185 million years laid out west to east.

title: Cross Dartmoor on a letterboxing walk
description: Hundreds of hidden stamp boxes scattered across the moor since 1854. Wild camping is legal here, which it is nowhere else in England.

title: Walk out to St Michael's Mount on the causeway
description: A tidal island with a castle, still lived in by the St Aubyn family. Walk out at low water and take the boat back.

title: See the biomes at the Eden Project
description: Two vast biome domes in a worked-out china clay pit, one rainforest, one Mediterranean. The rainforest canopy walkway is the bit to do.

title: Watch a play at the Minack Theatre
description: An open-air theatre cut into a granite cliff by one woman and her gardener from 1931 onwards, with the Atlantic as the backdrop.

title: Walk the white cliffs from Dover to South Foreland
description: Five kilometres of chalk clifftop to a Victorian lighthouse, with France visible on a clear day and peregrines on the face.

title: Watch seals at Blakeney Point
description: England's largest grey seal colony, with pups on the shingle from November. Boats run from Morston Quay on the tide.

title: See the Sutton Hoo ship burial site
description: The mounds where an Anglo-Saxon king was buried in a ship in the 620s, found in 1939 days before the war began.

title: Punt on the Cherwell in Oxford
description: Punting from the Cherwell Boathouse up past the Parks. Push off the bottom, do not let go of the pole, and expect to fall in once.

title: See the King's College chapel fan vault
description: The largest fan vault in the world, and the Christmas Eve carol service that the BBC has broadcast since 1928.

title: Swim on the rooftop at the Thermae Bath Spa
description: The only natural thermal water in Britain, in a Georgian city built entirely from the same honey-coloured stone.

title: Walk the best-preserved stretch of Hadrian's Wall
description: Steel Rigg to Housesteads runs along the crags where the wall still stands highest. Eighty Roman miles coast to coast if you want the lot.

title: Look up in the Northumberland dark sky park
description: The largest area of protected night sky in Europe, with an observatory in the forest and aurora on the better nights.

title: Cross the sands to Lindisfarne
description: A tidal causeway to Holy Island, with published safe crossing times and a refuge box for people who ignore them.

title: Walk the Malham Cove limestone pavement
description: A seventy-metre curved cliff with a field of clints and grikes on top, and peregrines nesting on the face in spring.

title: Ride the Settle to Carlisle railway
description: Seventy-two miles over the Ribblehead Viaduct and through Blea Moor, saved from closure by a public campaign in the 1980s.

title: Walk the Yorkshire Three Peaks in a day
description: Pen-y-ghent, Whernside and Ingleborough: 39 kilometres and 1,585 metres of ascent, traditionally inside twelve hours.

title: See Whitby Abbey above the harbour
description: The ruin Bram Stoker used for Dracula's landfall, reached by 199 steps from a town that still lands its own crab.

title: Ride the Blackpool heritage trams along the front
description: The oldest electric tramway in Britain, running since 1885, along seven miles of seafront and illuminations in autumn.

title: Row out to the island on Ullswater
description: The steamers have run since 1859. Take one to Howtown and walk the shore path back, which is the finest low-level walk in the Lakes.

title: Climb Scafell Pike from Wasdale
description: England's highest point at 978 metres, up from the deepest lake in the country. The Corridor Route is the interesting way.

title: Take the ferry across the Mersey
description: Fifty minutes on the river with the Three Graces on the skyline, and the song playing on the tannoy whether you want it or not.

title: Walk the Monsal Trail through the tunnels
description: Thirteen kilometres of former railway through four lit tunnels in the Peak District, flat enough for anyone and open to bikes.

title: Walk up Arthur's Seat before breakfast
description: An extinct volcano inside the city, 251 metres up, with the whole of Edinburgh and the Forth laid out at the top.

title: Find the closes off the Royal Mile
description: Narrow alleys running downhill off the spine of the old town, several of them buried under later buildings and open to tours.

title: Ride the Jacobite over the Glenfinnan Viaduct
description: A steam train from Fort William to Mallaig over the curved viaduct. Watching it from the hillside path is free and just as good.

title: Walk into Glen Coe on the Lost Valley path
description: A hanging valley the MacDonalds hid stolen cattle in, up a boulder scramble from the road. The massacre of 1692 happened below.

title: Climb Ben Nevis by the mountain track
description: Britain's highest at 1,345 metres. The summit plateau is in cloud most days and navigating off it has killed people; carry a compass.

title: Look for dolphins at Chanonry Point
description: Bottlenose dolphins feed in the narrows on a rising tide, close enough to the shingle spit to hear them breathe.

title: Walk the machair beaches of Harris
description: Luskentyre and Seilebost are white shell sand against turquoise water, and they are usually empty even in July.

title: Take a boat to Staffa and Fingal's Cave
description: Hexagonal basalt columns and a sea cave that gave Mendelssohn his overture. Puffins nest on the top in early summer.

title: Land on St Kilda
description: Forty miles beyond the Outer Hebrides, evacuated in 1930 and now the largest gannet colony in the North Atlantic. Weather cancels most trips.

title: Walk into the Neolithic village at Skara Brae
description: Older than the pyramids, with stone dressers and box beds still in place, uncovered by a storm in 1850.

title: Watch puffins at Sumburgh Head
description: Puffins nest within a few metres of the cliff path here from May to early August, which is unusually close for Britain.

title: Ride the funicular and walk the Cairngorm plateau
description: The largest area of arctic-alpine plateau in Britain, with reindeer, ptarmigan and weather that turns in minutes.

title: Kayak among the Slate Islands
description: Flooded slate quarries and the Corryvreckan whirlpool nearby, third largest in the world. Go with a guide for the tide.

title: Walk the Speyside whisky trail
description: Half of Scotland's distilleries in one river valley, linked by a walking route on an old railway line.

title: Walk a stage of the Pembrokeshire Coast Path
description: Two hundred and ninety kilometres around the only coastal national park in Britain, with more ascent overall than Everest.

title: Take the boat to Skomer for the puffins
description: Forty thousand puffins and the world's largest Manx shearwater colony. Landing numbers are capped; go on the first boat.

title: Ride the Ffestiniog narrow gauge railway
description: The oldest independent railway company in the world, built in 1836 to bring slate down to Porthmadog by gravity.

title: Cross the Devil's Bridge at the Aberglaslyn Pass
description: A river gorge path along an old railway ledge with chains bolted to the rock where the footing runs out.

title: Zip line over a slate quarry at Penrhyn
description: The fastest zip line in the world at over 160 kilometres an hour, strung across a working slate quarry.

title: Walk the walls of Conwy Castle town
description: Edward I's ring of castles, and the most complete set of medieval town walls in Britain still walkable end to end.

title: Walk the four waterfalls at Ystradfellte
description: You can walk behind Sgwd yr Eira, which drops over an overhang into a pool. The path is genuinely slippery all year.

title: Look for red kites at Bwlch Nant yr Arian
description: Red kites were down to a handful of Welsh pairs in the 1930s. A hundred and more now come in to feed here every afternoon.

title: Cross the Carrick-a-Rede rope bridge
description: A rope bridge thirty metres above the sea to a salmon fishermen's island. Timed tickets, and it closes in high wind.

title: Walk the Dark Hedges avenue
description: A beech avenue planted in the eighteenth century, now closed to traffic after too many people stopped in the middle of the road.

title: Walk the Mourne Wall in the Mournes
description: Thirty-five kilometres of drystone wall built over the summits between 1904 and 1922 to enclose a reservoir catchment.

title: Go underground at Marble Arch Caves
description: A show cave you enter partly by boat, on a global geopark that crosses the border into Cavan.

title: See Neuschwanstein from the Marienbrucke
description: Ludwig II's fantasy castle, unfinished when he died in 1886. The bridge over the gorge gives the view; the castle itself is timed-entry only.

title: Surf the standing wave on the Eisbach
description: A permanent river wave in the middle of the Englischer Garten, surfed around the clock and in the snow. Watching is free.

title: Drink in a Munich beer garden under the chestnuts
description: By Bavarian law you may bring your own food to a traditional beer garden and buy only the beer. The chestnut trees were planted to keep cellars cool.

title: Watch the Glockenspiel figures turn at Marienplatz
description: Forty-three bells and thirty-two figures re-enacting a 1568 wedding, at eleven and noon. It is gloriously slow.

title: Take the boat across the Konigssee
description: Electric boats only since 1909, so the lake is silent. The boatman stops halfway to play a trumpet at the cliff for the echo.

title: Ride up to the Eagle's Nest
description: A brass lift bored 124 metres up through the mountain to a Nazi-era teahouse, now a restaurant with an uneasy view.

title: Walk the Partnach Gorge
description: Seven hundred metres of tunnel and ledge cut through a gorge eighty metres deep. In winter it freezes into ice curtains.

title: Stand on the Zugspitze summit
description: Germany's highest point at 2,962 metres, reached by cable car or cog railway, with four countries visible on a clear day.

title: Walk the walls of Rothenburg ob der Tauber
description: A complete medieval walled town on the Romantic Road, with a covered walkway running most of the circuit.

title: Eat Nuremberg bratwurst three to a roll
description: Protected by law at seven to nine centimetres, grilled over beechwood and served three in a bun by street windows.

title: Walk the treetop canopy trail in the Bavarian Forest
description: A 1,300-metre walkway through the crowns of Germany's oldest national park, spiralling up a tower at the end.

title: Find the Wieskirche in a meadow
description: A rococo pilgrimage church standing alone in a field, so ornate inside that the plain exterior reads as a joke.

title: Go up the Reichstag dome
description: Foster's glass dome lets you look down into the parliament chamber below. Free, but you must register in advance.

title: Walk through the Holocaust memorial's stelae
place: Denkmal fur die ermordeten Juden Europas
description: Two thousand seven hundred and eleven concrete blocks on uneven ground. The information centre underneath is the harder half.

title: See the bust of Nefertiti on Museum Island
description: Five museums on one island in the Spree, including the Pergamon altar and a 3,300-year-old queen who needs no introduction.

title: Look for traces of the wall at the Mauerpark flea market
description: The death strip is now a Sunday flea market with open-air karaoke in the amphitheatre, which says most of what needs saying.

title: Swim in a lake inside the city at Wannsee
description: A 1,275-metre lido open since 1907, at the end of an S-Bahn line, and busy with Berliners rather than visitors.

title: See the Green Vault treasury in Dresden
description: August the Strong's treasure chamber, rebuilt after the firestorm. Timed entry to the historic rooms is capped at a hundred people an hour.

title: Hear Bach where he worked at the Thomaskirche
description: He was cantor here for twenty-seven years and is buried in the chancel. The boys' choir still sings the motet on Fridays.

title: Walk from Goethe's house to Buchenwald
description: Eight kilometres between the high point of German humanism and a concentration camp. Doing both in one day is the point.

title: See the Bauhaus building where modernism started
description: Gropius's 1926 school building, with the glass curtain wall that every office block since has borrowed from.

title: Punt the Spreewald canals
description: Two hundred channels through alder forest where the post is still delivered by boat, in the Sorbian-speaking corner of Germany.

title: Walk under the chalk cliffs at Jasmund
description: White cliffs above beech forest on the Baltic, painted by Caspar David Friedrich and protected as world heritage.

title: Watch cranes gather at the Muritz lakes
description: Tens of thousands of common cranes stage here each autumn before flying south. Dawn and dusk from the hides.

title: Climb the south tower of Cologne Cathedral
description: Five hundred and thirty-three steps up the tallest twin-spired church in the world, which took 632 years to finish.

title: Tour the Zollverein coal mine
description: The most beautiful coal mine in the world by its own reckoning, closed in 1986 and now world heritage, with a swimming pool in the coking plant.

title: Hear a concert in the Elbphilharmonie
description: A glass wave dropped on a brick warehouse, with a hall tuned by Yasuhisa Toyota. The public plaza halfway up is free.

title: Walk the Speicherstadt warehouse canals
description: The largest warehouse district in the world, on oak piles in the water, best at night when the brick is floodlit.

title: Get up early for the Fischmarkt
description: Sunday from five in the morning, half fish market and half the end of Saturday night, with a brass band in the auction hall.

title: Walk the Wadden Sea mudflats at low tide
description: A guided wattwanderung across the seabed to an island. The tide comes back faster than you can walk, so do not go alone.

title: Eat marzipan in Lubeck
description: The Hanseatic capital, with a brick gothic gate that is sinking, and the marzipan house that has been at it since 1806.

title: Walk the Rote Kliff on Sylt
description: Forty kilometres of North Sea beach on a thin island reached by a causeway train, with red cliffs at Kampen.

title: Ride the Schwarzwaldbahn through the Black Forest
description: Thirty-nine tunnels and a full spiral to gain height, engineered in the 1860s and still the scenic way across.

title: Walk to the Triberg waterfalls
description: Germany's best-known falls drop 163 metres in seven steps, through forest full of red squirrels that expect to be fed.

title: Cycle around Lake Constance
description: Two hundred and sixty kilometres through three countries on a signed lakeside route, with ferries to cut corners.

title: Walk the Philosophers' Way above Heidelberg
description: A steep path up the far bank with the ruined castle and the old bridge below. Hegel and Holderlin walked it, hence the name.

title: Walk the Calmont via ferrata above the Moselle
description: The steepest vineyard in Europe at 65 degrees, with ladders and cables bolted through it above a bend in the river.

title: Drink apfelwein in Sachsenhausen
description: Served from a grey stoneware bembel into ribbed glasses in taverns that hang a pine wreath out when the new batch is ready.

title: Be first through the gate at the Acropolis
description: The site opens at eight and the marble is lethal in the afternoon heat. The Parthenon has been under restoration since 1975 and will be for a while yet.

title: See the Parthenon marbles that are still in Athens
description: The top floor is laid out to the exact dimensions of the Parthenon, with plaster casts standing in for the pieces held in London.

title: Walk up Lycabettus for the sunset
description: Two hundred and seventy-seven metres above the city, with the Acropolis below and the Saronic Gulf beyond. A funicular runs if you would rather.

title: Eat your way through the Varvakios market
description: The central meat and fish market, with tavernas inside it that open at dawn and serve patsas to people finishing a night shift.

title: Watch the sun go down at the Temple of Poseidon
description: A fifth-century BC temple on a headland an hour from Athens. Byron carved his name into a column, which you should not copy.

title: Test the acoustics at the theatre of Epidaurus
description: Fourteen thousand seats, and a coin dropped in the orchestra is audible in the back row. Summer festival performances still use it.

title: Walk through the Lion Gate at Mycenae
description: The citadel of Agamemnon, with a beehive tomb outside the walls that held the largest unsupported span in Europe for a thousand years.

title: Explore the ghost city of Mystras
description: A Byzantine capital abandoned on a mountainside above Sparta, with frescoed churches and a palace scattered down the slope.

title: Drive the tower villages of the Mani
description: Stone tower houses built for blood feuds, on a bare limestone peninsula that stayed effectively independent for centuries.

title: Walk the stadium at ancient Olympia
description: The original stadium track is still there and you can run the length of it. The games ran here every four years for over a millennium.

title: Stand where the oracle spoke at Delphi
description: The Greeks considered this the navel of the world. The site climbs the mountainside, so the walk up is part of it.

title: Cross the stone bridges of the Zagori
description: Forty-six slate villages linked by arched packhorse bridges, above the Vikos gorge, which is among the deepest in the world.

title: Row to the island in Lake Pamvotida
description: A lake island with no cars, monasteries and the house where Ali Pasha was finally shot through the floorboards in 1822.

title: Ride the Pelion narrow gauge train
description: A 60-centimetre gauge line designed by the father of the painter de Chirico, winding through chestnut forest to the sea.

title: Walk to the summit of Mount Olympus
description: Two thousand nine hundred and eighteen metres, with a refuge halfway and a genuine scramble on the final summit of Mytikas.

title: Eat bougatsa in Thessaloniki in the morning
description: Filo pastry with semolina custard, dusted with icing sugar and cut up with scissors. Greece's second city takes breakfast seriously.

title: See the frescoes at Kastoria's Byzantine churches
description: Fifty-four surviving Byzantine churches around a lakeside town that made its money on fur, most of them small and unlocked on request.

title: Swim in the lagoon at Balos
description: Pink-tinged sand and shallow water at the top corner of Crete, down a rough track or by boat from Kissamos.

title: Walk the palace at Knossos
description: The Minoan palace Evans partly rebuilt in concrete, controversially. Go to the Heraklion museum afterwards for the originals.

title: Ride the boat to Spinalonga
description: A Venetian fortress island used as a leper colony until 1957, and the last one in Europe to close.

title: Walk the Preveli palm gorge to the beach
description: A freshwater river running through a palm forest to a beach, which is not a combination Greece offers often.

title: Climb to the unfinished kouros of Naxos
description: A ten-metre marble statue abandoned in the quarry where it cracked, lying on its back in an orchard since the seventh century BC.

title: Take a boat to Kleftiko on Milos
description: White volcanic rock formations and sea caves used by pirates, reachable only from the water.

title: Walk the medieval street of the Knights
description: The largest inhabited medieval town in Europe, built by the Knights Hospitaller and still lived in behind four kilometres of wall.

title: Arrive into Symi harbour by boat
description: Neoclassical houses in ochre and blue stacked around a horseshoe harbour, built on sponge money and barely altered since.

title: See the cave of the Apocalypse on Patmos
description: The cave where John is said to have received the Revelation, under a fortified monastery that has run since 1088.

title: Walk to the monastery on the cliff at Amorgos
description: A white monastery three metres deep and eight storeys tall, glued to a vertical cliff three hundred metres above the sea.

title: Swim at the Canal d'Amour on Corfu
description: Soft sandstone eroded into channels and arches on the north coast, with the swim-through the whole place is named for.

title: Look down on the shipwreck at Navagio
description: A smuggler's freighter beached in 1980 on white cliffs and blue water. The clifftop viewing platform has been moved for rockfalls.

title: Row on the underground lake at Melissani
description: The cave roof collapsed, so at midday the sun drops straight onto water that reads as electric blue.

title: Walk the petrified forest of Lesbos
description: Twenty-million-year-old sequoia trunks turned to stone by volcanic ash, standing upright where they grew.

title: Swim in the vathres rock pools of Samothraki
description: Granite plunge pools fed by waterfalls off Mount Saos, on an island with no airport and very little tourism.

title: Walk up to the Panagia above Chora
description: A zigzag path from a cliff-edge village to a whitewashed church, with the Aegean two hundred metres straight down.

title: Watch the light hit El Capitan in Yosemite Valley
description: Granite walls a kilometre high above a glacial valley. US national parks restrict dogs to paved areas and campgrounds only.

title: Climb the cables up Half Dome
description: 24km return with 1,460m of climb, finishing on two steel cables up bare granite. Permits are by lottery and people have died on the cables.

title: Catch the Horsetail Fall firefall in February
description: For about two weeks the setting sun lights a thin fall on El Capitan so it glows like molten rock. Needs water in the fall and a cloudless west horizon.

title: Stand under General Sherman in Sequoia National Park
description: The largest tree on earth by volume - 1,487 cubic metres, and still adding the equivalent of a mature tree's worth of wood every year.

title: Climb Mount Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48
description: 4,421m via 35km and 1,900m of ascent, usually done in one brutal day. Day-use permits are a February lottery.

title: Find the movie locations in the Alabama Hills
description: Rounded granite used in more than 400 films, with Mobius Arch framing Whitney behind it. BLM land, so dogs and free camping are both fine.

title: Walk among the tufa towers at Mono Lake
description: Calcium spires exposed when Los Angeles diverted the inflow streams and the lake dropped 14m. A court case in 1994 stopped it going dry.

title: Walk the streets of Bodie ghost town
description: A gold town of 10,000 abandoned to arrested decay - about 100 buildings left standing exactly as found, with goods still on the shop shelves.

title: Watch sunrise over the dunes in Death Valley
description: The hottest place ever reliably recorded at 56.7C, and the lowest in North America at 86m below sea level. Do not come in July.

title: Find the moving rocks at Racetrack Playa
description: Stones that leave trails across the dry lake, finally explained in 2014 as thin ice floating them along. 43km of tyre-shredding washboard to reach.

title: Sleep under the Joshua trees
description: Where the Mojave meets the Colorado desert, with monzogranite boulders, a Dark Sky Park designation and rock climbing everywhere you look.

title: Climb Salvation Mountain
description: Leonard Knight spent nearly thirty years building a hill out of adobe and half a million litres of donated paint, beside the shrinking Salton Sea.

title: Drive Highway 1 through Big Sur
description: 140km of coast road on the edge of the Santa Lucia range. Landslides close sections for months at a time - check before committing.

title: Walk the headlands at Point Lobos
description: Called the greatest meeting of land and water in the world by the painter Francis McComas - sea otters, harbour seals and Monterey cypress.

title: Tour the excess of Hearst Castle
description: 165 rooms built by William Randolph Hearst over 28 years, with a Roman pool lined in gold leaf and a zoo that once held zebras. Some still roam.

title: Stand under the tallest trees on earth in Redwood
description: Coast redwoods reach over 110m. The tallest known tree's location is deliberately unpublished to protect the ground around its roots.

title: Walk across the Golden Gate Bridge
description: 2.7km of art deco steel painted International Orange so it stays visible in fog. September and October are the clearest months.

title: Take the night tour of Alcatraz
description: A federal prison for 29 years, and occupied by Native American activists for 19 months from 1969 - graffiti from that occupation is still on the walls.

title: Ride a cable car up Hyde Street
description: The last manually operated cable car system in the world, running since 1873 by gripping a cable moving under the street at a constant 15km/h.

title: Walk among the old-growth at Muir Woods
description: One of the last uncut coast redwood stands near the coast, saved in 1908. Parking and shuttle must be reserved in advance - no walk-ups.

title: Taste Cabernet in the Napa Valley
description: The 1976 Judgement of Paris, where Napa beat Bordeaux blind, remade the region. Most tastings now need a booking.

title: See the city from Griffith Observatory
description: Free since it opened in 1935, with the Hollywood sign on one side and the whole basin on the other. Go at dusk and stay for the telescope.

title: Walk the Venice Beach boardwalk
description: Built in 1905 as a Californian imitation of Venice, canals included. Now street performers, Muscle Beach and a skate park on the sand.

title: See the tar pits at La Brea
description: Asphalt still seeping in the middle of Los Angeles, having trapped and preserved Ice Age animals for 50,000 years. Excavation continues on site.

title: Kayak the sea caves at La Jolla
description: Seven caves cut into the sandstone cliff, in a marine reserve with leopard sharks in the shallows through summer and sea lions on the rocks.

title: Spend a day in Balboa Park
description: 490 hectares of Spanish Colonial Revival buildings from the 1915 exposition, holding 17 museums and the San Diego Zoo.

title: Swim in Lake Tahoe
description: 501m deep and clear enough to see 20m down, straddling the California and Nevada line. Cold enough that most people manage about four minutes.

title: Look into Crater Lake
description: The deepest lake in the US at 594m, filling a caldera left when Mount Mazama collapsed about 7,700 years ago. Fed only by rain and snow.

title: Walk up to Multnomah Falls
description: 189m in two drops with a 1914 footbridge across the middle. Timed-entry permits apply in summer - book before you drive out.

title: Watch the tide come in at Haystack Rock
description: A 72m sea stack with tufted puffins nesting on it in spring and tide pools at its base. Oregon beaches are public and dog friendly by law.

title: Watch the sea drain into Thor's Well
description: A collapsed sea cave that appears to swallow the ocean. Best an hour either side of high tide - and people have been swept off these rocks.

title: See the Painted Hills change colour
description: Banded claystone recording 35 million years of climate change, and the colours genuinely shift with moisture and light through the day.

title: Climb Misery Ridge at Smith Rock
description: The birthplace of American sport climbing, on welded tuff above a river bend. The ridge trail is short, steep and named accurately.

title: Get lost in Powell's City of Books
description: A city block of new and used books shelved side by side - around a million of them, and the largest independent bookshop in the world.

title: Walk the Hoh Rain Forest in Olympic
description: A temperate rainforest getting up to 4 metres of rain a year, with moss hanging off every branch - and glaciers and coast in the same park.

title: Walk through Hole-in-the-Wall at Rialto Beach
description: Driftwood logs the size of telegraph poles, sea stacks in the mist, and an arch you can only reach at low tide. Check the tide table, seriously.

title: See the wildflowers at Paradise on Mount Rainier
description: An active volcano carrying more glacial ice than the rest of the lower 48 combined, with a six-week meadow bloom at its foot.

title: Watch the fish throwers at Pike Place Market
description: Trading since 1907, and one of the oldest continuously operating farmers markets in the country. The first Starbucks is across the street.

title: Look for resident orcas in the San Juan Islands
description: The Southern Resident orcas are down to about 73 animals and no longer reliably here - transient Bigg's killer whales are now the more likely sighting.

title: Stand above Palouse Falls
description: A 60m fall into a basalt bowl carved by the Missoula floods at the end of the last ice age. Best in spring melt, and the cliff edges are unfenced.

title: Take the bus into Denali
description: One 148km road into six million acres, and private vehicles are barred beyond mile 15. Grizzly, caribou, moose and wolf all along it.

title: Chase the northern lights from Fairbanks
description: Sitting under the auroral oval, with displays on roughly four nights in five when skies are clear between September and March.

title: Watch tidewater glaciers calve in Kenai Fjords
description: Nearly 40 glaciers flow off the Harding Icefield, several straight into the sea - the boat cuts its engines and you listen to the ice crack.

title: Watch bears fish at Brooks Falls
description: Brown bears catching salmon mid-air from a viewing platform in Katmai. Reachable only by float plane, and the subject of Fat Bear Week.

title: Cruise into Glacier Bay
description: Entirely covered by ice in 1794 and now open water for 100km - one of the fastest documented glacial retreats anywhere. Huna Tlingit homeland.

title: Drive the Dalton Highway to the Arctic Circle
description: 666km of mostly gravel built to service the oil pipeline, with three fuel stops on the entire route and no mobile coverage.

title: Ride the Alaska Railroad to Seward
description: Four hours from Anchorage through country with no road access at all, and one of the last railways anywhere you can flag down from the trackside.

title: Watch Kilauea glow after dark
description: One of the most active volcanoes on earth. Whether there is anything to see depends entirely on the current eruption - check the USGS status first.

title: Stargaze from Mauna Kea
description: 4,207m and the best-placed observatory site on earth. It is also sacred to Native Hawaiians, and telescope construction here remains contested.

title: Walk down to Papakolea green sand beach
description: One of only a handful of green sand beaches in the world, coloured by olivine from an eroding cinder cone. A hot 8km round trip on foot.

title: Watch sunrise from the Haleakala summit
description: 3,055m above the clouds, and about 3C at dawn. Sunrise entry needs a reservation booked up to 60 days ahead - there is no walk-up option.

title: Drive the Road to Hana
description: 620 curves and 59 one-lane bridges in 84km. Locals still use this road daily - pull over and let them past.

title: Snorkel the Molokini crater
description: A sunken volcanic crescent forming a sheltered crater with 45m visibility, and a marine reserve since 1977.

title: See the Na Pali Coast from the water
description: 27km of 1,200m cliffs with no road access at all. Boat, helicopter, or the Kalalau Trail - and that trail needs a permit and a head for heights.

title: Look into Waimea Canyon
description: Mark Twain reputedly called it the Grand Canyon of the Pacific - 16km long and 900m deep, cut into red volcanic rock.

title: Stand above the USS Arizona at Pearl Harbor
description: 1,177 crew died on the Arizona and most remain aboard. Oil still seeps from the wreck, a couple of drops a minute, eighty years on.

title: Learn to surf at Waikiki
description: Long, slow, forgiving waves and the beach where Duke Kahanamoku introduced surfing to the wider world. The gentlest place anywhere to start.

title: Walk the Strip after dark in Las Vegas
description: 6.8km of casinos built on a desert crossroads. Whatever you think of it, there is nowhere else quite like it, and walking it takes longer than it looks.

title: Find the petroglyphs at Valley of Fire
description: Nevada's oldest state park - Aztec sandstone in violent reds, with 3,000-year-old rock art at Atlatl Rock and the Fire Wave a short walk in.

title: See the Milky Way from Great Basin National Park
description: Some of the darkest skies left in the continental US, plus bristlecone pines that were already thousands of years old when Rome fell.

title: Drive the Extraterrestrial Highway
description: 158km of State Route 375 past the back gate of Area 51, with one small town, one bar and no fuel for long stretches.

title: Hike below the rim of the Grand Canyon
description: Going down is optional, coming back up is not - rangers pull people off the Bright Angel Trail every summer. Go in spring or autumn.

title: Reach the quieter North Rim of the Grand Canyon
description: Takes about a tenth of the visitors, sits 300m higher, and closes under snow from December. Four hours' drive from the South Rim to go 16km.

title: Raft the Colorado through the Grand Canyon
description: Up to three weeks and 440km through the canyon floor. Private permits run on a weighted lottery with a wait that has run to years.

title: Walk down to Havasu Falls
description: Turquoise water from travertine minerals, 16km down into Havasupai land. Permits sell out within minutes on the February release and are non-transferable.

title: See the light beams in Antelope Canyon
description: A slot canyon on Navajo Nation land, accessible only with a Navajo guide. The shafts of light appear around midday from about March to October.

title: Stand above Horseshoe Bend
description: A 270-degree meander of the Colorado, 300m below an unfenced sandstone rim. Twenty minutes from the car park, and no shade at all.

title: Drive the valley floor at Monument Valley
description: A Navajo tribal park, not a national park - the sandstone buttes John Ford filmed nine times. The 27km loop road is rough but doable in a normal car.

title: Win the lottery for The Wave at Coyote Buttes
description: Undulating Navajo sandstone laid down as dunes 190 million years ago. Only 64 people a day get in, by lottery, and the route is unmarked.

title: Climb Cathedral Rock at sunset in Sedona
description: Iron-stained sandstone spires, a serious short scramble, and a town built around the belief that the rocks emit energy vortexes.

title: Walk among the saguaro at sunset
description: Saguaro grow only in the Sonoran, take 35 years to flower and 75 to sprout an arm. The tallest here are over 12m.

title: See the fossil logs at Petrified Forest
description: 225-million-year-old trees turned to quartz, plus a stretch of original Route 66. One of the very few national parks where dogs can join you on trails.

title: Drive the surviving stretches of Route 66
description: Decommissioned in 1985 and replaced by interstates, but long segments survive as business routes through towns the freeway bypassed.

title: Look into Meteor Crater
description: 1.2km wide and 170m deep, punched out 50,000 years ago and the first crater on earth proven to be from an impact. Apollo crews trained in it.

title: Wade The Narrows in Zion
description: Walking up the Virgin River between 300m walls that close to nine metres apart. Closed whenever flash flood risk is high - check daily.

title: Walk the chains up Angels Landing
description: A 500m spine with chains and drops on both sides. Permits have been required since 2022, by lottery, and the fatality count is in the teens.

title: Walk down among the hoodoos at Bryce Canyon
description: Not a canyon but an eroding escarpment holding the densest concentration of hoodoos on earth. The Navajo Loop takes you between them.

title: Walk to Delicate Arch for sunset
description: The arch on Utah's licence plates - 4.8km return over slickrock with no shade. Arches has held over 2,000 arches and loses one occasionally.

title: Watch sunrise through Mesa Arch at Canyonlands
description: For about twenty minutes at dawn the underside of the arch glows orange from light bouncing off the canyon below.

title: Drive the Burr Trail through Capitol Reef
description: A 160km wrinkle in the earth's crust called the Waterpocket Fold, and the least visited of Utah's five parks. Pick fruit in the Fruita orchards in season.

title: Wander the mushroom rocks at Goblin Valley
description: A valley of squat hoodoos you are actually encouraged to scramble over - rare in a landscape this fragile, and excellent for it.

title: Drive on the Bonneville Salt Flats
description: About 120 square kilometres of salt crust where land speed records have been set since 1912. Wet for much of the year - check before driving on.

title: Find Spiral Jetty on the Great Salt Lake
description: Robert Smithson's 460m basalt coil from 1970, submerged for thirty years and now high and dry as the lake shrinks - which is its own commentary.

title: Sled the gypsum dunes at White Sands
description: 275 square miles of white gypsum sand you can toboggan down. Dogs are allowed on leash almost everywhere here, unusually.

title: Watch the bat flight at Carlsbad Caverns
description: Hundreds of thousands of Brazilian free-tailed bats spiral out of the natural entrance at dusk. Walk in through the same hole rather than taking the lift.

title: Climb the ladders to the cliff dwellings at Bandelier
description: Ancestral Pueblo homes carved into volcanic tuff, occupied for four centuries. Wooden ladders take you up into the alcoves themselves.

title: Walk the adobe streets of Santa Fe
description: Founded in 1610 and the oldest capital in the US, with a building code that has kept the whole centre in adobe. Georgia O'Keeffe's museum is here.

title: Visit Taos Pueblo
description: Continuously inhabited for over 1,000 years - the oldest such community in the US, and still without electricity or running water by choice.

title: See the dishes at the Very Large Array
description: 27 radio dishes, each 25m across, moved along rail tracks into different configurations across a high desert plain. Contact was filmed here.

title: Drive Trail Ridge Road in Rocky Mountain National Park
description: The highest continuous paved road in the US, topping 3,713m, with eighteen kilometres above the treeline. Timed entry applies in summer.

title: See the Maroon Bells reflected at dawn
description: Reputedly the most photographed peaks in North America, and lethal to climb - the mudstone is so loose they are known as the Deadly Bells.

title: Sandboard the Great Sand Dunes
description: The tallest dunes in North America at 230m, against the Sangre de Cristo range, with a seasonal creek at their base you can float down in spring.

title: Tour the Cliff Palace at Mesa Verde
description: 150 rooms built into an alcove by Ancestral Puebloans around 1200 CE and abandoned within a century. Ranger-guided entry only, ladders included.

title: Drive the Million Dollar Highway to Ouray
description: 40km of US 550 over three passes with no guardrails and a sheer drop on the outside lane. Built on an 1880s toll road for the silver mines.

title: Look into the Black Canyon of the Gunnison
description: So narrow and deep that parts of the floor get 33 minutes of sunlight a day. The Painted Wall is the tallest cliff in Colorado at 682m.

title: Watch the Grand Prismatic Spring from the overlook
description: The world's first national park, sitting on an active supervolcano. The overlook trail beats the boardwalk for seeing the colours.

title: Watch wolves at dawn in the Lamar Valley
description: Wolves were reintroduced in 1995 after seventy years' absence, and this valley is where you have the best chance. Bring a spotting scope and get up early.

title: Wait for Old Faithful to go off
description: Erupts every 60 to 110 minutes and is predicted to within ten minutes - the most predictable big geyser anywhere, though not the largest.

title: Paddle Jenny Lake under the Tetons
description: The range rises 2,100m straight off the valley floor with no foothills at all, because the fault runs right along its base.

title: Walk the base trail around Devils Tower
description: The first US national monument, declared in 1906. Sacred to more than twenty tribes, who ask climbers to stay off voluntarily through June.

title: Drive the Going-to-the-Sun Road in Glacier
description: 80km over Logan Pass, only fully open for about ten weeks a year, and now requiring a timed entry reservation in peak season.

title: Walk the Highline Trail along the Garden Wall
description: Cut into a cliff along the Continental Divide, with a hand cable on the exposed opening section and mountain goats using the same path.

title: Walk the lava fields at Craters of the Moon
description: 1,600 square kilometres of basalt flows and lava tubes, last erupted about 2,000 years ago. Apollo astronauts trained here in 1969.

title: See Shoshone Falls at full flow
description: At 65m it is higher than Niagara, but irrigation takes most of the water for much of the year - spring runoff is the only time it performs.

title: Walk to Sawtooth Lake
description: A granite range with over 400 alpine lakes and no road through the middle of it, in one of the largest dark-sky reserves in the country.

title: Walk the Notch Trail in Badlands
description: A wooden ladder up a cliff face leads to a ledge over the White River valley, through eroded sediment laid down 75 million years ago.

title: See the faces at Mount Rushmore
description: Carved 1927-41 into a granite face in the Black Hills - land the Supreme Court ruled in 1980 was taken from the Lakota unlawfully.

title: Drive the Wildlife Loop in Custer State Park
description: A herd of around 1,400 bison, plus the Needles Highway with tunnels cut so tight they have to be measured before you drive them.

title: See the wild horses in Theodore Roosevelt National Park
description: The only national park named for a person, on the ranch land that turned him into a conservationist. Feral horses and bison on the loop road.

title: Walk into Santa Elena Canyon at Big Bend
description: 460m limestone walls with the Rio Grande running between them - the US on one bank, Mexico on the other, close enough to shout across.

title: Watch 1.5 million bats leave Congress Avenue Bridge
description: The largest urban bat colony in the world, roosting in bridge expansion joints and pouring out at dusk from March to October.

title: Queue for brisket in Texas Hill Country
description: Post oak, salt, pepper and about twelve hours. The best places sell out by early afternoon and the queue starts before they open.

title: Walk the River Walk and the Alamo
description: A flood control scheme from the 1930s turned into a river-level promenade, linking to four Spanish missions that are World Heritage listed.

title: Ride into Palo Duro Canyon
description: The second largest canyon in the US, 190km long and up to 240m deep, and almost nobody outside Texas knows it exists.

title: Wait for the Marfa lights
description: Unexplained lights reported since 1883, with a purpose-built viewing area on US 90 - and a town that became a minimalist art destination because Donald Judd moved in.

title: Kayak beneath the cliffs at Pictured Rocks
description: 60m sandstone cliffs on Lake Superior, streaked blue, orange and green by mineral seepage. The lake is cold enough to be genuinely dangerous.

title: Run down the dune climb at Sleeping Bear
description: A 137m sand bluff above Lake Michigan. Going down takes two minutes; coming back up takes most people close to an hour.

title: Cycle around car-free Mackinac Island
description: Motor vehicles have been banned since 1898, so everything moves by horse, bicycle or foot. The shore road is a flat 13km loop.

title: Portage a canoe through the Boundary Waters
description: More than 1,000 lakes linked by portage trails, with motors banned across most of it. You carry the canoe over your head between the water.

title: Walk into the Apostle Islands ice caves
description: Sea caves hung with icicles, reachable on foot only when the lake freezes solid enough - which has happened just a handful of times this century.

title: Take the architecture cruise on the Chicago River
description: The city rebuilt after the 1871 fire and invented the skyscraper doing it. The river was also reversed in 1900 so it flows away from the lake.

title: See your reflection in Cloud Gate
description: Anish Kapoor's 110-tonne stainless steel bean, welded from 168 plates with every seam polished away.

title: Ride the tram to the top of the Gateway Arch
description: 192m of stainless steel catenary curve, ascended in a tram of tilting five-person pods designed in two weeks in 1960.

title: See the exhibits at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
place: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
description: In Cleveland because a DJ here popularised the term in the early 1950s. I M Pei designed the glass pyramid on the lakefront.

title: Go underground at Mammoth Cave
description: Over 685km mapped and still growing - by a wide margin the longest cave system known anywhere, and more than twice the next longest.

title: Follow the Kentucky Bourbon Trail
description: Around 95% of the world's bourbon is made in Kentucky, ageing in charred new oak in warehouses you can walk through and smell from the road.

title: Watch the synchronous fireflies in the Smokies
description: For about two weeks each June, one firefly species here flashes in unison. Access is by lottery, and it is worth entering.

title: Hear a songwriter round in Nashville
description: Broadway is the loud version; the Bluebird Cafe and the writers' rounds are where the songs actually get made, in rooms of ninety people.

title: Stand in the studio where Elvis recorded at Sun
description: A single small room where Elvis, Johnny Cash, Carl Perkins and Jerry Lee Lewis all recorded. Still a working studio at night.

title: Visit the National Civil Rights Museum at the Lorraine Motel
description: Built around the balcony where Martin Luther King Jr was killed in 1968. Room 306 is preserved exactly as it was that afternoon.

title: Follow the brass bands down Frenchmen Street
description: Where locals go when tourists go to Bourbon Street - live jazz in a dozen rooms within three blocks, most nights of the year.

title: Take a boat into the Atchafalaya swamp
description: The largest wetland and swamp in the US - bald cypress hung with Spanish moss, alligators, and a way of life built entirely on the water.

title: Walk the squares of Savannah
description: Laid out in 1733 around 24 public squares, 22 of which survive, under live oaks hung with Spanish moss.

title: See the wild horses on Cumberland Island
description: A barrier island reachable only by ferry, with feral horses on the dunes and the ruins of a Carnegie mansion in the maritime forest.

title: Paddle the mangroves in the Everglades
description: A river 100km wide and 15cm deep, and the only place where alligators and crocodiles share territory. Go in the dry season for the wildlife.

title: Drive the Overseas Highway to Key West
description: 180km over 42 bridges to the southernmost point in the continental US, built on the piers of Flagler's railway destroyed by a hurricane in 1935.

title: Snorkel the fort moat at Dry Tortugas
description: 113km west of Key West by ferry or seaplane - a vast unfinished brick fort on a sand key, with coral growing along the moat wall.

title: Watch a rocket launch from the Space Coast
description: Launch cadence is now high enough that a week here will usually catch one. The Saturn V hanging in the visitor complex is a real one.

title: Snorkel with manatees at Crystal River
description: The only place in the US where supervised in-water encounters with manatees are legal - they gather in the 22C springs when the gulf turns cold.

title: Walk the Battery in Charleston
description: Antebellum houses along the seawall, and the harbour where the Civil War began at Fort Sumter in 1861.

title: Drive the Blue Ridge Parkway in autumn
description: 755km of ridge road with no commercial traffic and a 72km/h limit. The colour moves down the mountain about 30m a day through October.

title: Climb the Cape Hatteras lighthouse
description: 257 steps up the tallest brick lighthouse in the US, on a barrier island so mobile the whole structure was moved 880m inland in 1999.

title: Walk the catwalk under the New River Gorge Bridge
description: A 24-inch catwalk 260m above the river, under the bridge deck. One day each October it is legal to BASE jump off the top.

title: Drive Skyline Drive through Shenandoah
description: 170km along the Blue Ridge crest with 75 overlooks. One of the few national parks where dogs are allowed on almost every trail.

title: Watch the pony swim at Chincoteague
description: Feral ponies swim the channel between islands each July, herded by the volunteer fire brigade who have run it since 1925.

title: Spend a day in the Smithsonian museums
description: Nineteen museums, all free, including Air and Space and the National Museum of African American History and Culture - the last needs timed passes.

title: Walk the memorials on the National Mall after dark
description: Lincoln, Vietnam and Korea are all open 24 hours and lit at night, when they are far quieter and considerably more affecting.

title: See the cherry blossom at the Tidal Basin
description: 3,000 trees given by Tokyo in 1912. Peak bloom lasts a few days and the date is forecast each year - it has been trending earlier for decades.

title: Tour Fallingwater
description: Frank Lloyd Wright cantilevered a house directly over a waterfall in 1935. Tours must be booked and sell out weeks ahead in autumn.

title: See the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall
description: Both the Declaration and the Constitution were debated in the same room. Free timed tickets, and the queue moves faster than it looks.

title: Walk Pickett's Charge at Gettysburg
description: Crossing the mile of open field the Confederate infantry walked into artillery fire in 1863 tells you more than any museum can.

title: Walk the High Line end to end
description: A disused elevated freight line turned 2.3km linear park through Manhattan's west side. Free, and dogs are not permitted.

title: Cross the Brooklyn Bridge on foot at dawn
description: The first steel-wire suspension bridge, opened 1883. Walk Brooklyn to Manhattan at first light and you will have the promenade to yourself.

title: Spend an afternoon in the Met
description: Two million works across 5,000 years, including an entire Egyptian temple moved stone by stone. Pick two wings and accept you will miss the rest.

title: Eat your way through a New York deli
description: Pastrami cured for weeks and steamed for hours, in rooms that have not been redecorated since the 1950s and are better for it.

title: Count the waterfalls at Watkins Glen
description: Nineteen waterfalls in three kilometres, on a stone path cut into the gorge that goes behind, under and over the water.

title: See all three falls at Letchworth
description: Called the Grand Canyon of the East - a 27km gorge with 180m walls and three major waterfalls, and hot air balloons over it in autumn.

title: Walk the Freedom Trail in Boston
description: 4km of red brick line through sixteen sites, from Boston Common to the Bunker Hill Monument, taking in most of the American Revolution.

title: Cycle the Cape Cod Rail Trail
description: 40km of flat former railway through pitch pine and cranberry bog, with the Atlantic dunes of the National Seashore at the far end.

title: See the first sunrise in the US from Cadillac Mountain
description: From October to March this is the first place in the continental US to catch the sun. Acadia is unusually dog-friendly for a national park.

title: Climb the iron rungs of the Beehive Trail
description: Iron rungs and narrow ledges bolted to a granite cliff, climbed in one direction only. Short, and not for anyone uneasy about exposure.

title: Eat a lobster roll on a working wharf
description: Maine lands most of the country's lobster. The argument over warm butter versus cold mayonnaise is genuine and locals hold firm views.

title: Drive the Kancamagus Highway in October
description: 55km through the White Mountain National Forest with no petrol, no shops and no phone signal - just sugar maples doing their thing.

title: Ride the cog railway up Mount Washington
description: The world's first mountain-climbing cog railway, running since 1869, up a summit that held the world land wind speed record at 372km/h for sixty years.

title: Chase the autumn colour through Vermont
description: Sugar maples turn earliest and brightest here, and the state runs a foliage tracker because the peak moves south about 50km a week.

title: Walk the Newport Cliff Walk past the mansions
description: 5.6km between Gilded Age summer houses and the Atlantic, with public access preserved by colonial-era shoreline rights the owners have fought for a century.

title: Cross the Edmund Pettus Bridge at Selma
description: Where marchers were beaten on Bloody Sunday in 1965, an event that moved the Voting Rights Act through Congress within months.

title: Drive the Natchez Trace Parkway
description: 715km following a path used for thousands of years, with no commercial traffic and sections of the original sunken trace you can walk.

title: Dig for diamonds at Crater of Diamonds
description: The only diamond-bearing site in the world open to the public where you keep what you find. Several hundred are found each year, most of them small.

title: Canoe on Moraine Lake in Banff
description: Rock flour suspended in glacial meltwater gives that colour. Private vehicles are now banned on the Moraine Lake road - shuttle only.

title: Drive the Icefields Parkway to Jasper
description: 232km past more than 100 glaciers between Lake Louise and Jasper - routinely called one of the great drives anywhere.

title: Stargaze in Jasper's Dark Sky Preserve
description: One of the largest accessible dark sky preserves in the world, with a decent chance of aurora on clear winter nights.

title: Walk the sea floor at Hopewell Rocks
description: The highest tides on earth, up to 16m. You walk on the ocean floor at low tide and kayak over the same spot six hours later.

title: Drive the Cabot Trail in autumn
description: 298km around Cape Breton's highlands, through Acadian and Gaelic communities, at its best when the maples turn in early October.

title: See polar bears at Churchill
description: Bears gather here waiting for Hudson Bay to freeze. There is no road in - you arrive by train or plane, and go out in a tundra buggy.

title: Visit the Watchmen sites on Haida Gwaii
description: Standing mortuary poles at SGang Gwaay, guarded by Haida Watchmen and deliberately left to return to the earth. Access is permitted and limited.

title: Take the boat under Horseshoe Falls
description: Around 2,800 cubic metres a second go over the Horseshoe. The Canadian side has the view; the boat gets you into the spray.

title: Walk the walled old town of Quebec City
description: The only walled city north of Mexico, founded 1608, and the most convincingly European place in North America.

title: Drive the Dempster Highway to the Arctic Ocean
description: Around 900km of gravel from Dawson City to Tuktoyaktuk on the Arctic Ocean. Carry two spare tyres - this is not an exaggeration.

title: Cycle the Stanley Park seawall
description: A 9km flat loop around a 400-hectare forest on a downtown peninsula, past totem poles and under the Lions Gate Bridge.

title: Cross the Capilano Suspension Bridge
description: 137m of swaying cedar plank 70m above a river gorge, first strung across in 1889. The free Lynn Canyon bridge nearby does much the same job.

title: Eat your way around Granville Island Public Market
description: An industrial sandbar turned market and artist quarter under a bridge, reached by tiny rainbow-coloured ferries that hold about twelve people.

title: Drive the Sea to Sky Highway to Whistler
description: 120km along Howe Sound with the water on one side and granite on the other, past Shannon Falls and the Stawamus Chief.

title: Climb the Stawamus Chief at Squamish
description: One of the largest granite monoliths in the world, climbed by chains and ladders to three summits above Howe Sound.

title: Hike to the Joffre Lakes
description: Three stacked glacial lakes in improbable turquoise. Day passes are required, and the park now closes for periods so Lil'wat and N'Quatqua Nations can harvest.

title: Ride the Peak 2 Peak gondola at Whistler
description: The largest ski resort in North America, linked by a gondola with the longest unsupported span in the world at over 3km between towers.

title: Storm-watch at Tofino in winter
description: People book rooms specifically to watch Pacific storms hit Long Beach. Surfing here happens year-round in a thick wetsuit.

title: Walk the rainforest trails in Pacific Rim National Park
description: Old-growth Sitka spruce and western red cedar on boardwalks over bog, with the West Coast Trail running south for 75 gruelling kilometres.

title: See the Butchart Gardens near Victoria
description: Built inside an exhausted limestone quarry from 1904 onward by the cement magnate's wife, and now a national historic site.

title: Look for the spirit bear in the Great Bear Rainforest
description: The Kermode bear is a white-coated black bear found almost nowhere else - maybe 400 exist. Access is through First Nations-led operators only.

title: Taste ice wine in the Okanagan Valley
description: Canada's warmest wine region, on a desert lake, and the source of most of the world's ice wine - pressed from grapes frozen on the vine.

title: Paddle to Emerald Lake in Yoho
description: Takakkaw Falls drops 254m in the same park, and the Burgess Shale here holds the best-preserved Cambrian fossils found anywhere.

title: Canoe on Lake Louise beneath the Victoria Glacier
description: Get there before seven or the car park is full by eight. In winter the lake freezes hard enough to skate and they carve an ice castle on it.

title: Walk on the Athabasca Glacier at the Columbia Icefield
description: The largest icefield in the Rockies, feeding three oceans. Markers along the approach road show where the glacier stood each decade - it is a sobering walk.

title: Ride the gondola at Banff for the Bow Valley view
description: Up Sulphur Mountain to a boardwalk along the summit ridge, with hot springs at the bottom that started the whole national park system in 1885.

title: See the dinosaur collection at the Royal Tyrrell Museum
description: One of the largest dinosaur collections in the world, in Drumheller, because the badlands around it are among the richest fossil beds anywhere.

title: Walk the hoodoos at Dinosaur Provincial Park
description: World Heritage listed, and more than 400 dinosaur skeletons have come out of it - many still lie exposed where they eroded out.

title: Visit Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
description: Blackfoot peoples drove bison off this cliff for nearly 6,000 years. The interpretive centre is built into the hillside and told from their perspective.
