title: Walk the Red Rock Canyon in Waterton Lakes
description: Joined to Montana's Glacier as the world's first International Peace Park, where prairie runs straight into mountain with no foothills between.

title: Go to the Calgary Stampede
description: Ten days of rodeo, chuckwagon racing and pancake breakfasts every July, with the whole city in boots. Running since 1912.

title: Hear the silence in Grasslands National Park
description: A Dark Sky Preserve of mixed-grass prairie with reintroduced bison and black-tailed prairie dogs, and almost no light or noise for a hundred kilometres.

title: Snorkel with beluga whales at Churchill
description: Around 57,000 belugas move into the Churchill River estuary each summer. They are curious enough to come and inspect a snorkeller.

title: Do the EdgeWalk on the CN Tower
description: A hands-free walk on a 1.5m ledge around the outside of the tower at 356m, tethered to an overhead rail. The tallest such walk in the world.

title: Swim at the Grotto on the Bruce Peninsula
description: A limestone sea cave on Georgian Bay with water clear enough to be mistaken for the Caribbean, and roughly ten degrees colder than it looks.

title: Canoe and portage through Algonquin Park
description: 2,400 lakes linked by portage, with wolf howls answered on organised August nights and maples that turn the whole park red in late September.

title: Skate the Rideau Canal in Ottawa
description: 7.8km of frozen canal used as a commuter route, with beavertail pastry stands on the ice. Warming winters mean some years it barely opens at all.

title: Cruise the Thousand Islands
description: Actually 1,864 islands in the St Lawrence, split between Canada and the US - one holds the shortest international bridge in the world.

title: Eat a smoked meat sandwich and a bagel in Montreal
description: Boiled in honey water and baked in a wood oven, the Montreal bagel is a genuinely different thing from the New York version - and locals will explain why.

title: Walk up Mont Royal for the city view
description: Designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, who also did Central Park. Sunday afternoons in summer bring the tam-tams - an open drum circle on the east slope.

title: Stand at the foot of Montmorency Falls
description: 83m, higher than Niagara, with a suspension bridge across the lip and a via ferrata up the cliff beside it.

title: Watch belugas in the Saguenay Fjord
description: One of the longest fjords in the world outside Scandinavia, with a resident and endangered beluga population, plus blue whales at the confluence.

title: Walk to Perce Rock at low tide
description: A 400m limestone wall with an arch through it, walkable from shore at low tide, with the world's most accessible gannet colony on the island beyond.

title: Photograph the lighthouse at Peggy's Cove
description: A working fishing village on granite scoured bare by glaciers. People are swept off the black rocks near the water most years - stay on the light-coloured stone.

title: Walk the painted waterfront at Lunenburg
description: A World Heritage town laid out on a 1753 British grid, still in its original wooden buildings, and home port of the schooner on the Canadian dime.

title: Visit Green Gables on Prince Edward Island
description: The farmhouse that inspired Anne of Green Gables, on an island of red sand cliffs where the book still drives a good part of the economy.

title: Walk on the earth's mantle at the Tablelands
description: Peridotite from the earth's mantle, forced to the surface by continental collision. So toxic to plants that it looks like Mars - and it helped prove plate tectonics.

title: Boat into Western Brook Pond
description: A landlocked fjord with 600m walls, reached by a 3km bog walk before the boat. The water is so pure it barely conducts electricity.

title: Watch icebergs drift past Iceberg Alley
description: Ice calved off Greenland glaciers 10,000 years ago, drifting down the Labrador Current. Locals chip it out for gin, and there is a public tracking map.

title: Stand among the puffins at Elliston
description: One of the closest land-based puffin viewing sites in North America - the birds nest on a stack a few metres from where you stand.

title: See the Norse settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows
description: The only confirmed Norse site in North America, occupied around 1021 CE - five hundred years before Columbus, and dated precisely by a solar storm.

title: Climb Signal Hill above St John's
description: Where Marconi received the first transatlantic wireless signal in 1901, above a harbour entrance called the Narrows and a street of painted row houses.

title: Drink the Sourtoe cocktail in Dawson City
description: A gold rush town with wooden boardwalks and a bar that drops a mummified human toe into your drink. The rule is your lips must touch it.

title: Fly over the Kluane icefields
description: Canada's highest peak and the largest non-polar icefield on earth, almost none of it reachable on foot. The flightseeing run is the only realistic way in.

title: Raft past Virginia Falls in Nahanni
description: One of the first four sites ever added to the World Heritage list, in 1978. Virginia Falls is twice the height of Niagara, and access is by float plane only.

title: Watch the aurora from Yellowknife
description: Directly under the auroral oval with a flat horizon and very dry winter air - statistically among the most reliable aurora viewing anywhere on earth.

title: Reach the floe edge on Baffin Island
description: The line where sea ice meets open water, travelled by snowmobile and qamutik sled with Inuit guides - narwhal, bowhead and polar bear all use it.

title: Swim in a cenote near Valladolid
description: Thousands of limestone sinkholes over a flooded cave system, sacred to the Maya and the peninsula's only natural fresh water.

title: Hear the Kukulkan pyramid echo at Chichen Itza
description: Clap at the base of El Castillo and the staircase returns a chirp said to imitate the quetzal. Twice a year a serpent shadow runs down the steps.

title: Ride El Chepe through Copper Canyon
description: A canyon system deeper and four times larger than the Grand Canyon, crossed by a railway with 37 bridges and 86 tunnels.

title: Eat your way through the Oaxaca markets
description: Seven moles, tlayudas, mezcal and chapulines - widely held to be the best regional cooking in Mexico, and it is not close.

title: Meet grey whales in San Ignacio Lagoon
description: Grey whales calve here and mothers routinely push their calves up to the boats to be touched - one of the strangest wildlife encounters anywhere.

title: Snorkel the reef at Akumal
description: Part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the second largest on earth, with green turtles grazing the seagrass close to shore.

title: Climb the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan
description: A city of over 100,000 people that was already ruins when the Aztecs found it and named it the place where gods were born. Summit access varies - check on arrival.

title: See the Aztec Sun Stone at the Museo Nacional de Antropologia
description: Widely rated among the best museums in the world - the 24-tonne Sun Stone, the Maya collection, and a courtyard fountain shaped like an umbrella.

title: Ride a trajinera through the canals of Xochimilco
description: The last surviving stretch of the Aztec canal and floating-garden system, with painted boats, mariachi for hire and the unsettling Isla de las Munecas.

title: Visit the Casa Azul, Frida Kahlo's house
description: The cobalt house in Coyoacan where she was born and died, kept as she left it. Tickets must be booked online and sell out days ahead.

title: See a lucha libre bout at Arena Mexico
description: Masked wrestling in a 16,000-seat cathedral of the sport, where the crowd's insults are half the performance. Friday nights are the big card.

title: Eat tacos al pastor from a spinning trompo
description: Lebanese shawarma technique applied to marinated pork, carved onto a small tortilla with pineapple flicked on top. Mexico City's defining street food.

title: Stand in the Zocalo and the Templo Mayor beside it
description: One of the largest city squares in the world, built directly over Tenochtitlan - the Aztec temple was found in 1978 by electricity workers digging a trench.

title: Climb the ruins at Uxmal
description: Puuc-style Maya architecture with an oval-based pyramid found nowhere else, and a fraction of the crowds at Chichen Itza an hour away.

title: Swim in the cenote at Ik Kil
description: An open cenote 26m down with vines hanging to the water. Busy - the quieter ones near Valladolid are better if you have a car.

title: Watch flamingos at Rio Lagartos
description: A biosphere reserve holding tens of thousands of American flamingos, plus a pink salt lagoon coloured by the same algae as Australia's Hutt Lagoon.

title: Walk the Paseo de Montejo in Merida
description: A boulevard of mansions built on the henequen fibre boom, in a city repeatedly ranked among the safest in the Americas.

title: See the Maya ruins at Tulum above the sea
description: The only major Maya city built on the coast, walled on three sides, on a cliff above a beach you can swim from. Go at opening to beat both heat and buses.

title: Float the canals at Sian Ka'an
description: A World Heritage biosphere where you drift down ancient Maya-dug canals wearing a life jacket, carried by the current through mangrove.

title: Dive the cenote at Dos Ojos
description: Part of one of the longest underwater cave systems on earth, with halocline layers where fresh and salt water meet and the view goes blurry.

title: Swim with whale sharks off Isla Mujeres
description: One of the largest whale shark aggregations in the world gathers off the Yucatan each summer - hundreds of animals feeding on tuna spawn.

title: Dive the underwater sculpture museum at MUSA
description: More than 500 concrete figures sunk off Cancun by Jason deCaires Taylor, built from pH-neutral marine cement so coral colonises them.

title: Boat through the Sumidero Canyon
description: Walls up to 1,000m high on the Grijalva River, with crocodiles on the banks and a moss formation shaped like a Christmas tree.

title: Reach the jungle ruins of Palenque
description: Maya architecture at its most refined, still half-swallowed by rainforest with howler monkeys overhead. Pakal's tomb was found intact under the main temple.

title: Swim the turquoise cascades at Agua Azul
description: Limestone-rich water over travertine terraces gives the colour - though it browns after heavy rain, so the dry season is the only time it lives up to the name.

title: Spend a few days in San Cristobal de las Casas
description: A highland colonial town at 2,200m, and the centre of Tzotzil and Tzeltal Maya life - the church at nearby San Juan Chamula is unlike anywhere else.

title: Stand on the terraces at Monte Alban
description: A Zapotec capital built by levelling an entire mountaintop around 500 BCE, looking out over three valleys.

title: See the petrified waterfall at Hierve el Agua
description: Mineral springs have built a rock formation that looks exactly like a frozen waterfall, with infinity pools at the top. Access is sometimes closed by local disputes.

title: Spend Dia de Muertos in Oaxaca
description: Comparsas through the streets and families keeping vigil in the cemeteries. It is a family occasion, not a festival - go quietly and ask before photographing.

title: Watch turtles nest at Mazunte
description: A former turtle slaughtering village that reinvented itself as a conservation centre after the 1990 ban - olive ridleys now arrive in mass arribadas.

title: Tour an agave distillery in Tequila
description: The blue agave landscape here is World Heritage listed. A plant takes seven years to mature, and only spirit made in this region may use the name.

title: Hear mariachi in Plaza Garibaldi's home town
description: Mariachi, tequila and charreria all originate in Jalisco. The Hospicio Cabanas here holds Orozco murals painted across its chapel ceiling.

title: Wander the tunnels and alleys of Guanajuato
description: A silver city built in a ravine, where the roads run through former river tunnels under the town and the houses are painted every colour available.

title: Watch the light on the Parroquia in San Miguel de Allende
description: A neo-Gothic pink church designed by a self-taught stonemason from postcards of European cathedrals, in a World Heritage colonial town.

title: Eat mole poblano where it was invented
description: Twenty or more ingredients including chocolate and several chillies, ground for hours. Also the home of chiles en nogada, eaten in the two months poblano chillies are in season.

title: Find the church on top of the Great Pyramid of Cholula
description: By volume the largest pyramid on earth, so overgrown the Spanish mistook it for a hill and built a church on the summit in 1594.

title: Swim at Playa Balandra near La Paz
description: A shallow turquoise bay you can wade most of the way across, with daily visitor caps to protect it. Frequently voted Mexico's best beach.

title: See El Arco at Cabo San Lucas
description: A granite arch at the very tip of the Baja peninsula, where the Sea of Cortez meets the Pacific. Reachable only by water taxi.

title: Dive with sea lions at Espiritu Santo
description: A World Heritage island in the sea Cousteau called the aquarium of the world, with a sea lion colony that plays with snorkellers.

title: Stand in the monarch butterfly forests of Michoacan
description: Hundreds of millions of monarchs arrive after a 4,000km migration and cover the oyamel firs so densely the branches bend.

title: Climb the pyramid of the Niches at El Tajin
description: 365 recessed niches, one for each day. The voladores still perform outside - five men descending from a 30m pole on ropes, a rite recognised by UNESCO.

title: Ride the Basaseachi trail in the Copper Canyon
description: Mexico's second-highest waterfall at 246m, in Raramuri country - the people known for running enormous distances in sandals cut from tyres.

title: Cross Lake Atitlan between the villages
description: A caldera lake ringed by three volcanoes and a dozen Maya villages, each with its own dialect and dress, connected only by boat.

title: Watch sunrise over the canopy from Temple IV at Tikal
description: Maya temples pushing up through rainforest, with howler monkeys roaring in the dark before dawn. The view from Temple IV was used as a rebel base in Star Wars.

title: Watch Semana Santa carpets in Antigua
description: Coloured sawdust laid into elaborate street carpets overnight, then destroyed by the procession walking over them at dawn.

title: Climb Acatenango to watch Fuego erupt
description: An overnight climb to 3,976m to camp opposite an active volcano that erupts every twenty minutes through the night. Cold, steep and unforgettable.

title: Swim the limestone pools at Semuc Champey
description: A natural limestone bridge carrying turquoise pools over a river that runs underneath it. The road in is genuinely rough and takes hours.

title: Dive the Great Blue Hole
description: A 318m-wide collapsed cave system 124m deep, with stalactites at 40m proving it was dry land during the last ice age. Advanced certification required.

title: Snorkel with rays at Hol Chan and Shark Ray Alley
description: A cut through the Belize Barrier Reef - the largest in the northern hemisphere - where nurse sharks and southern stingrays gather in waist-deep water.

title: Wade into the ATM cave at Actun Tunichil Muknal
description: You swim into a cave to reach Maya sacrificial remains calcified into the floor, including the Crystal Maiden. Cameras have been banned since one was dropped on a skull.

title: Soak in the hot springs under Arenal
description: A near-perfect cone that erupted continuously from 1968 until 2010 and is now dormant. The river running off it is naturally heated to bath temperature.

title: Walk the hanging bridges in the Monteverde cloud forest
description: Founded by Quaker pacifists who left the US in 1951. Resplendent quetzals nest here, and the forest is permanently inside the cloud layer.

title: Look for tapirs in Corcovado
description: National Geographic called it the most biologically intense place on earth - all four Costa Rican monkey species, plus tapir, jaguar and scarlet macaw.

title: Watch green turtles nest at Tortuguero
description: The most important green turtle nesting site in the western Caribbean, reachable only by boat or small plane through a network of jungle canals.

title: Zip-line through the Guanacaste canopy
description: Canopy zip-lining was invented in Costa Rica in the 1970s as a way for biologists to study the treetops, and became an industry by accident.

title: Watch a ship transit the Panama Canal locks
description: Around 14,000 ships a year lifted 26m over the isthmus by gravity-fed locks. The Miraflores visitor centre puts you level with the deck of a passing vessel.

title: Sail the San Blas islands with the Guna
description: 365 islands governed autonomously by the Guna, who set their own visitor rules and sell molas - reverse-applique panels sewn by hand.

title: Find the red frogs on Isla Bastimentos
description: Strawberry poison dart frogs that vary in colour island to island - a textbook case of populations diverging in isolation.

title: Volcano board down Cerro Negro
description: You walk up an active black cinder cone carrying a plywood board, then sit on it and slide down the ash at up to 90km/h.

title: Cycle between the two volcanoes of Ometepe
description: An hourglass island formed by two volcanoes rising out of a freshwater lake, with pre-Columbian petroglyphs on the lower slopes.

title: Look into the lava lake at Masaya
description: One of very few volcanoes on earth where you can drive to the rim and look directly down at moving lava. Visits are timed and short for good reason.

title: Learn to dive on Utila
description: Among the cheapest places in the world to get certified, on the Mesoamerican Reef, with whale sharks passing through much of the year.

title: Read the hieroglyphic stairway at Copan
description: 63 steps carrying around 2,200 glyphs - the longest Maya inscription known, and the finest stone carving anywhere in the Maya world.

title: Surf the point at El Tunco
description: Consistent right-hand point breaks over rock and black sand, on a coast that has quietly become one of Central America's best surf destinations.

title: Drive the Ruta de las Flores
description: 36km through coffee highlands and five colonial towns, with weekend food fairs and murals on nearly every wall in Ataco.

title: Ride a 1950s American car through Havana
description: Kept running for seventy years on improvised parts after the 1962 embargo cut off imports. Habana Vieja around them is World Heritage listed.

title: Ride through the tobacco fields of Vinales
description: Limestone mogotes rising straight out of a valley farmed by ox and plough, producing the tobacco that goes into Cuba's best cigars.

title: Walk the cobbled streets of Trinidad
description: A sugar-boom town frozen since the 1850s, with pastel houses, a live-music staircase every night, and steam trains into the Valle de los Ingenios.

title: Climb Dunn's River Falls
description: 180m of travertine terraces climbed hand-in-hand in a human chain, with the sea right at the bottom of them.

title: Walk the Blue Mountain Peak trail for sunrise
description: A 2am start to 2,256m, where on a clear morning you can see Cuba. The coffee grown on these slopes is among the most expensive in the world.

title: Visit the Bob Marley Museum in Kingston
description: His home and studio at 56 Hope Road, kept as it was, with the bullet holes from the 1976 assassination attempt still in the wall.

title: Swim with the pigs at Big Major Cay
description: Feral pigs that swim out to meet boats on an uninhabited cay. Nobody agrees how they got there, and overfeeding has killed several - follow the guides.

title: Dive the blue holes of Andros
description: The largest concentration of blue holes on earth, inland and offshore, beside the third-longest barrier reef in the world.

title: Watch humpbacks in Samana Bay
description: Thousands of North Atlantic humpbacks come here to breed each winter - one of the largest and most reliable gatherings anywhere.

title: Swim at Bahia de las Aguilas
description: 8km of undeveloped white sand inside a national park, reached by boat or a rough track - and protected from resort building so far.

title: Kayak the bioluminescent bay at Mosquito Bay
description: The brightest recorded bioluminescent bay in the world - dinoflagellates light up around the paddle. Go on a new moon, and never with sunscreen on.

title: Walk to La Mina Falls in El Yunque
description: The only tropical rainforest in the US national forest system, full of coqui frogs whose call is on every Puerto Rican recording ever made.

title: Walk the walls of Old San Juan
description: Blue cobblestones cast from iron ballast, and El Morro - a six-level fortress that held off Drake and stood for four centuries.

title: Swim with turtles off Carlisle Bay
description: A marine park with six shipwrecks in shallow water and a resident hawksbill turtle population, right off the capital.

title: Go down into Harrison's Cave
description: A limestone cavern toured by electric tram, with a 12m waterfall inside it and stalactites still actively forming.

title: Play mas at Trinidad Carnival
description: The carnival that soca and steelpan came from, and the template most Caribbean carnivals copy. J'ouvert starts at 4am covered in mud and paint.

title: Snorkel the Buccoo Reef and Nylon Pool
description: A protected reef with a waist-deep sandbar pool a kilometre offshore, named by Princess Margaret for water she said was clear as nylon.

title: Climb Gros Piton
description: 770m of volcanic plug straight up out of the sea, guided only. The two Pitons together are the most recognisable silhouette in the Caribbean.

title: Bathe in the sulphur springs at Soufriere
description: Billed as the world's only drive-in volcano - a collapsed caldera you drive into, with mud baths people coat themselves in.

title: Walk to the Boiling Lake in Dominica
description: The second largest hot lake on earth, at the end of six hours through the Valley of Desolation. The Nature Isle has 365 rivers and almost no beaches.

title: Swim with sperm whales off Dominica
description: Resident family groups live off this coast year-round, and Dominica is one of the only countries to license in-water encounters with them.

title: Stand in the shallows at Stingray City
description: Southern stingrays gather on a waist-deep sandbar in the North Sound, a habit that started when fishermen cleaned their catch there decades ago.

title: Snorkel the wall at Grace Bay
description: Repeatedly voted the best beach in the world, protected by a barrier reef so there is no seaweed and almost no swell.

title: Find the natural pool in Arikok National Park
description: A desert island of cacti and divi-divi trees bent permanently by the trade winds, with a rock-enclosed tidal pool reachable only by 4WD or on foot.

title: Walk Nelson's Dockyard at English Harbour
description: The only continuously working Georgian naval dockyard in the world, built by enslaved labour and now World Heritage listed.

title: Dive the underwater sculpture park off Grenada
description: The world's first underwater sculpture park, installed in 2006 to draw divers away from reefs damaged by Hurricane Ivan - and now a reef itself.

title: Squeeze through The Baths on Virgin Gorda
description: House-sized granite boulders forming tidal grottoes and passages you scramble and swim through between two beaches.

title: Follow the underwater trail at Trunk Bay
description: A marked snorkelling trail with underwater signs identifying the coral, in a national park covering roughly two thirds of St John.

title: Climb to the Citadelle Laferriere
description: The largest fortress in the Americas, built after independence by the world's first free Black republic to repel a French return that never came.

title: Dive off Atauro Island
description: Surveys here recorded the highest average reef fish diversity yet measured anywhere in the world, an hour by ferry from Dili.

title: Cross to uninhabited Jaco Island
description: Considered sacred, so nobody stays overnight - local fishermen take you across the strait at the far eastern tip of Timor-Leste.

title: Walk the Campuhan Ridge at first light in Ubud
description: A 2km grass ridge between two rivers, quiet before seven and unbearably hot after nine. The obvious first morning in Ubud.

title: See the Tegallalang rice terraces before the buses
description: Terraces watered by subak, a cooperative irrigation system run by temple priests since the ninth century and now World Heritage listed.

title: Get robbed by macaques in the Sacred Monkey Forest
description: Around 1,200 long-tailed macaques in a temple complex in the middle of town. They will take sunglasses, phones and anything shiny - leave it in the room.

title: Bathe in the holy springs at Tirta Empul
description: A purification ritual Balinese Hindus have performed since 962 CE. Sarong required, and the queue moves spout by spout in a set order.

title: Watch a Legong performance in Ubud Palace
description: Gamelan and masked dance in the palace courtyard nearly every evening - a living tradition rather than a tourist show, and cheap.

title: Climb Mount Batur for sunrise
description: A 2am start up an active volcano to watch the sun come up over Lombok. Local guides are effectively compulsory and the trail is enforced as such.

title: See the lake temple at Ulun Danu Beratan
description: A water temple appearing to float on Lake Beratan in the highlands, dedicated to the goddess of lakes and rivers. It is on the 50,000 rupiah note.

title: Walk between the Jatiluwih rice terraces
description: Far larger and far quieter than Tegallalang, with walking loops through working terraces rather than a viewpoint you photograph from a cafe.

title: Swim under Sekumpul Falls
description: Seven falls dropping into one gorge in north Bali, reached by several hundred steps and a river crossing. Widely rated the island's best.

title: Watch the sunrise gate at Lempuyang
description: The Gates of Heaven framing Mount Agung. The famous reflection is a mirror held under a phone by the photographer - everyone queues for hours for it anyway.

title: Snorkel the USAT Liberty wreck at Tulamben
description: A torpedoed US cargo ship pushed off the beach by the 1963 Agung eruption, now lying 30m from shore in water shallow enough to snorkel.

title: Explore the water palace at Tirta Gangga
description: Stepping stones across carp ponds in a royal water garden built in 1946, rebuilt after Agung buried it seventeen years later.

title: Watch the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu at sunset
description: A sea temple on a 70m cliff, with a chanting circle of about seventy men performing the Ramayana as the sun goes down behind them.

title: Learn to surf the beach break at Canggu
description: Black volcanic sand, forgiving waves at Batu Bolong, and the centre of gravity for Bali's remote-working scene.

title: Surf or watch the reef break at Uluwatu
description: You paddle out through a cave in the cliff. A world-class left over shallow reef, and unforgiving of anyone who overestimates themselves.

title: Eat babi guling in a warung
description: Spit-roast suckling pig stuffed with turmeric, lemongrass and chilli - a ceremonial dish that most warungs sell out of by early afternoon.

title: Look down on Kelingking Beach from the cliff
description: A headland shaped like a dinosaur on Nusa Penida. The descent to the sand is a near-vertical scramble on bamboo rails - people are hurt on it regularly.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Nusa Penida
description: Reef mantas visit a cleaning station here year-round. The swell can be heavy, and the boat ride out is not for anyone prone to seasickness.

title: Cycle the flat lanes of Nusa Lembongan
description: Seaweed farms, a yellow suspension bridge to Nusa Ceningan, and a fraction of the traffic of Penida next door.

title: Watch dawn break over Borobudur
description: The largest Buddhist temple on earth, built around 800 CE and abandoned for centuries under volcanic ash. Climbing to the upper terraces is now capped and guided.

title: Walk the temple complex at Prambanan
description: A ninth-century Hindu complex of towering candi, badly damaged in the 2006 earthquake and still under restoration. The Ramayana ballet runs here in the dry season.

title: See batik being drawn by hand in Yogyakarta
description: A sultanate city and the cultural centre of Java, where batik tulis is still drawn line by line with a wax pen rather than stamped.

title: Watch sunrise over Mount Bromo from Penanjakan
description: A smoking cone inside a caldera called the Sea of Sand, with Semeru erupting on the horizon behind it. A 3am jeep and genuinely cold at altitude.

title: See the blue fire at Kawah Ijen
description: Ignited sulphuric gas burning electric blue in the dark, above a turquoise acid lake. Gas masks are essential, and miners still carry 80kg of sulphur out by hand.

title: Ride to the crater rim at Tumpak Sewu
description: A 120m curtain of water in a horseshoe amphitheatre. The descent to the base is bamboo ladders and rope in permanent spray - hard, and slippery.

title: Eat your way through a Jakarta street food night
description: Nasi goreng, satay, martabak and kerak telor from carts that appear after dark, in a city of ten million with a food scene drawn from every island.

title: Look into the crater lake at Kawah Putih
description: A pale turquoise sulphur lake in a crater above Bandung, sitting at 2,400m so the air is cool and faintly acidic.

title: Track Komodo dragons on Rinca
description: The largest lizard on earth at up to 3m, found wild on five islands and nowhere else. Rangers carry forked sticks, which is less reassuring in person.

title: Climb Padar Island for the three-bay view
description: About 800 steps to a ridge overlooking three crescent bays, each with differently coloured sand. The most photographed view in eastern Indonesia.

title: Snorkel the pink sand at Komodo
description: Red organ-pipe coral fragments mixed through white sand give the colour - one of only a handful of genuinely pink beaches anywhere.

title: See the three coloured lakes of Kelimutu
description: Three crater lakes that independently change colour - red, green, black, turquoise - as their mineral chemistry shifts. Local belief holds they receive the dead.

title: Climb Mount Rinjani to the crater rim
description: 3,726m, usually done over three days with porters, to a crater holding a lake and a new cone growing inside it. Genuinely hard, and closed in the wet.

title: Snorkel with turtles off Gili Trawangan
description: Three car-free islands where transport is bicycle or horse cart, with green turtles grazing in water shallow enough to snorkel from the beach.

title: Surf the point at Kuta Lombok
description: A string of horseshoe bays with reef breaks for every level, and a fraction of Bali's crowds despite the airport being twenty minutes away.

title: Dive Raja Ampat, the richest reef on earth
description: Surveys record over 1,500 fish and 550 coral species - the highest marine biodiversity ever measured. Getting there takes two flights and a boat.

title: Climb Piaynemo for the karst lagoon view
description: A boardwalk and 320 steps to a platform above a scatter of mushroom-shaped karst islets - the view that defines Raja Ampat in photographs.

title: Dive the wall at Bunaken
description: A vertical coral wall dropping to well over 1,000m, with visibility routinely past 30m and turtles at almost every depth.

title: Muck dive the Lembeh Strait
description: Black volcanic sand rather than coral, and the best critter diving in the world - mimic octopus, hairy frogfish, blue-ringed octopus, all on one dive.

title: Attend a Torajan funeral ceremony
description: Funerals here last days and can happen years after death, with the deceased kept at home in the meantime. Visitors are genuinely welcomed - bring a gift and a guide.

title: Trek to see orangutans at Bukit Lawang
description: Sumatran orangutans in the wild on the edge of Gunung Leuser - one of only two places on earth where the species survives, and it is critically endangered.

title: Stay on Samosir Island in Lake Toba
description: The largest volcanic lake on earth, filling a caldera left by an eruption 74,000 years ago that may have nearly wiped out early humans.

title: Surf the Mentawai Islands
description: Reeled-off perfect reef breaks reached by charter boat from Padang, and among the most consistent waves anywhere in the world.

title: Island-hop the Karimunjawa archipelago
description: 27 islands in a marine park off Java's north coast, most uninhabited, reached by a slow ferry that puts most travellers off entirely.

title: Walk the Siq into the Treasury at Petra
description: A 1.2km slot canyon opens onto a facade carved into the rock face by the Nabataeans around 2,000 years ago. Go at opening, before the canyon fills.

title: Climb the 800 steps to the Monastery at Petra
description: Larger than the Treasury and far quieter, because most visitors stop before the climb. A tea shack at the top looks out over the Wadi Araba.

title: Sleep in a Bedouin camp in Wadi Rum
description: Sandstone and granite towers in red desert, run by Bedouin tribes who hold the tourism rights. Stood in for Mars in half a dozen films.

title: Float in the Dead Sea
description: 430m below sea level, the lowest land on earth, and about ten times saltier than the ocean. It is also shrinking by roughly a metre a year.

title: Walk the colonnaded street at Jerash
description: One of the best-preserved Roman provincial cities anywhere, buried by earthquake and sand until the 1920s - the oval forum is almost intact.

title: Walk the Dana Biosphere Reserve
description: Jordan's largest reserve, dropping 1,500m from highland to desert through four biogeographic zones, on a village-run conservation model.

title: Dive the Red Sea reefs at Aqaba
description: Jordan's only coastline, 27km of it, with reefs unusually resilient to bleaching and a deliberately sunk C-130 Hercules at 17m.

title: Go up the Burj Khalifa at sunset
description: 828m and still the tallest building in the world by a wide margin. Book the sunset slot weeks ahead - it is the only one that consistently sells out.

title: Ride a 4WD over the dunes on a desert safari
description: Dune bashing, sandboarding and a camp dinner in the Al Marmoom reserve. Genuinely rough - not a good idea straight after eating.

title: Haggle in the Dubai gold and spice souks
description: Reached by abra across Dubai Creek for about a dirham. Roughly ten tonnes of gold sits in the windows at any time, and the price is always negotiable.

title: Visit the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
description: Holds 40,000 worshippers, with the largest hand-knotted carpet in the world on its floor. Free, and modest dress is provided at the entrance.

title: See the rain of light at Louvre Abu Dhabi
description: Jean Nouvel's 180m dome filters sun through eight layered star patterns, casting a shifting pattern of light on the galleries below.

title: Ride the world's longest zip line at Jebel Jais
description: 2.83km at up to 150km/h, flown head-first off the UAE's highest peak. The mountain road up is itself worth the drive.

title: Swim and climb through Wadi Shab
description: A boat across, 45 minutes on foot, then three pools to swim before squeezing through a crack in the rock to a waterfall inside a cave.

title: Walk the Balcony Walk on Jebel Shams
description: A ledge path along the rim of Wadi Ghul, called the Grand Canyon of Arabia, ending at an abandoned village cut into the cliff.

title: Camp in the Sharqiya Sands
description: Dunes up to 100m in bands of orange and white, still grazed by Bedouin herders. You let tyre pressure down at the edge and drive in.

title: Sail a dhow through the Musandam fjords
description: Sheer limestone inlets called the Norway of Arabia, on a peninsula separated from the rest of Oman by the UAE, with dolphins in the channels.

title: Go to the Friday goat market at Nizwa
description: Livestock paraded in a ring before dawn buyers, beside a 17th-century fort with a round tower built to survive cannon fire.

title: Watch green turtles nest at Ras al Jinz
description: One of the most important green turtle nesting sites in the Indian Ocean, with guided night and dawn visits from a reserve on the easternmost point of Arabia.

title: See Salalah green during the khareef
description: The monsoon turns a desert province green for three months a year - waterfalls, fog and the frankincense trees that made this coast rich.

title: Walk the Old City of Jerusalem
description: One square kilometre holding sites central to Judaism, Christianity and Islam. It sits in East Jerusalem, which most of the world regards as occupied territory.

title: Climb Masada for sunrise over the Dead Sea
description: A fortress on a desert plateau where a Jewish garrison held out against Rome until 73 CE. The Snake Path takes about an hour in the dark.

title: Float on the Sea of Galilee
description: Actually a freshwater lake, and the lowest on earth. The surrounding hills hold Capernaum and the Mount of Beatitudes.

title: Walk the Bauhaus White City in Tel Aviv
description: About 4,000 Bauhaus buildings put up by architects who fled Europe in the 1930s - the largest concentration anywhere, and World Heritage listed.

title: See Banksy's Walled Off Hotel in Bethlehem
description: A hotel built facing the separation wall, billed as having the worst view in the world, beside the Church of the Nativity. Entry is via Israeli checkpoint.

title: Walk the excavations at Jericho
description: Tell es-Sultan has evidence of settlement going back roughly 11,000 years, which makes it a contender for the oldest continuously inhabited place on earth.

title: Float over Cappadocia in a balloon at dawn
description: Up to 150 balloons lift at once over volcanic fairy chimneys. Flights are cancelled for wind more often than people expect - allow spare mornings.

title: Go down into the Derinkuyu underground city
description: Eighteen storeys cut into soft tuff, capable of sheltering 20,000 people with livestock, ventilation shafts and rolling stone doors.

title: Stand under the dome of the Hagia Sophia
description: Built as a cathedral in 537, converted to a mosque in 1453, a museum in 1935 and back to a mosque in 2020. Its dome went unmatched for a thousand years.

title: Get lost in the Grand Bazaar
description: Around 4,000 shops on 61 covered streets, trading since 1461 and among the oldest shopping complexes still operating anywhere.

title: Walk barefoot on the terraces at Pamukkale
description: White travertine terraces built by calcium-rich springs over millennia. Shoes are banned to protect them, and the Roman city of Hierapolis sits on top.

title: Walk the marble street at Ephesus
description: One of the largest Roman sites in the Mediterranean, with the Library of Celsus facade and a theatre that seated 25,000.

title: Watch sunrise among the heads on Mount Nemrut
description: Two-metre stone heads toppled from their bodies on a 2,134m summit, built as a tomb by a king who declared himself a god.

title: See the carved pillars at Gobekli Tepe
description: Monumental stone circles raised around 9500 BCE - roughly 6,000 years before Stonehenge, and by people who had not yet started farming.

title: See the Nabataean tombs at Hegra
description: Saudi Arabia's first World Heritage site - 111 tombs cut by the same civilisation that built Petra, and visited by a fraction of the numbers.

title: Stand at the Edge of the World near Riyadh
description: A 300m escarpment on the Tuwaiq cliffs where the plateau simply stops and an ancient seabed runs to the horizon. 4WD access only.

title: Walk the mud-brick city at Diriyah
description: At-Turaif, the original seat of the Saudi state, built in Najdi mud-brick and World Heritage listed since 2010.

title: Eat and haggle in Souq Waqif
description: Rebuilt in the traditional style on a centuries-old trading site, with a falcon souq and hospital in the middle of it.

title: See the collection at the Museum of Islamic Art
description: I M Pei came out of retirement at 91 to design it, on its own island so nothing could ever be built against it.

title: Drive to the inland sea at Khor Al Adaid
description: One of very few places on earth where the sea reaches into the heart of a desert, on the Saudi border and reachable only by 4WD across dunes.

title: Stand among the columns at Baalbek
description: The largest Roman temple complex ever built, with foundation stones over 800 tonnes that nobody has fully explained the moving of.

title: Take the boat through the Jeita Grotto
description: Two limestone caverns stacked over each other, the upper holding the largest known stalactite in the world at 8.2m, the lower toured by boat.

title: Walk the harbour at Byblos
description: Occupied for around 7,000 years and a candidate for the oldest continuously inhabited city. The Greek name for it gave us the word Bible.

title: Find the Tree of Life in the Bahraini desert
description: A mesquite standing alone in the desert for around 400 years with no obvious water source, roughly two kilometres from anything else.

title: Walk the layers at Qal'at al-Bahrain
description: A tell holding 4,000 years of continuous occupation, from the Dilmun civilisation up to a Portuguese fort on the top layer.

title: Go up the Kuwait Towers
description: Three towers finished in 1979, clad in eight million enamelled steel discs, badly damaged during the 1990 invasion and rebuilt afterwards.

title: Walk down Main Street at the original Disneyland
description: The only park Walt Disney personally walked, opened in 1955 on a former orange grove. Two parks now, and the Anaheim original is still the smallest.

title: Do all four parks at Walt Disney World
description: Magic Kingdom, EPCOT, Hollywood Studios and Animal Kingdom across 100 square kilometres - roughly the size of San Francisco, and its own governing district.

title: Ride the Hogwarts Express between Universal's two parks
description: The train only runs if you hold a park-to-park ticket, and the view out the window differs depending on which direction you travel. Epic Universe opened in 2025.

title: Take the studio backlot tram at Universal Studios Hollywood
description: A working studio with a theme park attached rather than the other way round - the tram runs through sets still used for filming.

title: Ride every coaster at Cedar Point
description: Seventeen roller coasters on a sand spit in Lake Erie, and widely regarded by enthusiasts as the best coaster collection anywhere on earth.

title: Survive the coaster count at Six Flags Magic Mountain
description: Twenty roller coasters, more than any park in the world, including one that launches you to 160km/h in under four seconds.

title: Ride the Dollywood coasters through the Smokies
description: Repeatedly voted the best theme park in the world by industry awards, built around Appalachian craft, bluegrass and Dolly Parton's own foundation.

title: Eat the fried chicken at Knott's Berry Farm
description: America's first theme park, which grew out of a roadside berry stand and a chicken dinner restaurant that still has the longest queue on site.

title: Ride through the chocolate factory town at Hersheypark
description: Built in 1906 as a picnic ground for chocolate factory workers. The streetlights in town are shaped like Hershey's Kisses, and the whole place smells of it.

title: Ride the Leviathan at Canada's Wonderland
description: Canada's largest park, with more roller coasters than anywhere outside the US, built around an artificial mountain you can walk inside.

title: Float the underground rivers at Xcaret
description: An eco-archaeological park built over Mayan ruins, where you snorkel through cave rivers and finish with a three-hour show of Mexican regional dance.

title: See the castle at Disneyland Paris
description: Le Chateau de la Belle au Bois Dormant is the most elaborate of all the Disney castles, with a stained-glass gallery upstairs and a dragon in the dungeon below.

title: Ride the wooden coasters at Parc Asterix
description: France's home-grown answer to Disney, built around the comic books, and locally regarded as having far better roller coasters.

title: Work through the countries at Europa-Park
description: Germany's largest park and repeatedly voted the world's best, laid out as eighteen European countries with thirteen coasters between them.

title: Ride Taron at Phantasialand
description: Famously cramped, because the park cannot expand outwards - so it builds upward and through itself, producing some of the most intense theming anywhere.

title: Wander the fairy tale forest at Efteling
description: Older than Disneyland, opened in 1952 around an illustrated fairy tale wood, and still the most atmospheric park in Europe after dark.

title: Ride the wooden coaster at Tivoli Gardens
description: Open since 1843 in the middle of Copenhagen. Walt Disney visited twice and took notes; its 1914 wooden coaster still carries a brakeman on every train.

title: Visit Bakken, the oldest amusement park in the world
description: Operating since 1583, when a spring was discovered here and entertainers followed the crowds. Free to enter, and set in a royal deer park.

title: Ride Helix at Liseberg
description: Scandinavia's largest park, built on a hillside so the coasters run down natural terrain, and transformed into a Christmas market each December.

title: Ride Nemesis at Alton Towers
description: Planning rules capped ride height at the treeline, so the coasters were dug into the ground instead - which is why Nemesis runs through a trench.

title: Ride Shambhala at PortAventura
description: Six themed worlds on the Costa Daurada, with one of Europe's tallest coasters and a Ferrari Land next door.

title: Spend a day at Gardaland
description: Italy's largest park, on the shore of Lake Garda, with a SeaLife aquarium attached and a genuinely good pirate dark ride.

title: Ride Journey to the Center of the Earth at Tokyo DisneySea
description: DisneySea exists nowhere else and is widely held to be the most beautifully themed park ever built - a volcano at its centre that actually erupts.

title: Visit Super Nintendo World at Universal Studios Japan
description: The first Super Nintendo World anywhere, where a wristband lets you collect coins by punching blocks around the land.

title: Ride the coasters under Mount Fuji at Fuji-Q Highland
description: Several record-breaking coasters with Fuji filling the horizon, plus a haunted hospital attraction that takes about an hour to walk through.

title: Ride the Mystic Manor at Hong Kong Disneyland
description: The smallest Disney park, but home to Mystic Manor - a trackless dark ride built here because Chinese custom made a haunted house a poor fit.

title: Take the cable car over the headland at Ocean Park
description: Half marine park, half thrill park, split across a headland and joined by a cable car and a funicular through the rock.

title: See the largest Disney castle at Shanghai Disneyland
description: The Enchanted Storybook Castle is the biggest Disney has built and the only one belonging to no single princess. Opened 2016, and Tron runs here best.

title: Ride the T Express at Everland
description: South Korea's largest park, with one of the steepest wooden coasters in the world and a tulip festival that draws as many people as the rides.

title: Skate the indoor rink at Lotte World
description: The largest indoor theme park on earth, with an outdoor island section on a lake, connected by monorail and open whatever the weather does.

title: Spend a day at Universal Studios Singapore
description: Compact enough to do properly in one day, on a resort island reached by cable car, monorail or a boardwalk you can simply walk across.

title: Ride Formula Rossa at Ferrari World
description: The fastest roller coaster in the world at 240km/h, which is quick enough that riders are issued safety goggles before boarding.

title: Ride the Wild Mouse at Luna Park Sydney
description: Under the Harbour Bridge since 1935, behind a giant grinning face. The 1959 Wild Mouse is one of the last of its kind still running anywhere.
